## E27 — The acquisition `provider` is rebuilt on every access, and `capabilities` / `isConfigured` are read from view bodies
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** low _(was medium)_ · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Acquisition/AcquisitionManager.swift:104–109`

```swift
    var provider: AcquisitionProviding {
        Self.makeProvider(activePlugin)
    }

    var capabilities: AcquisitionCapabilities { provider.capabilities }
    var isConfigured: Bool { provider.isConfigured }
```

**Problem.** `app.acquisitionCapabilities` and `app.acquisitionConfigured` are read directly inside
`body` in `BrowseAlbumDetailView` (464, 525, 879, 1011, 1066), `ArtistPageView` (344, 952),
`SettingsSections` (334–338), `DiscoverySearchView` (2096, 2101, 1505) and `ServerPlaylistViews`
(2244). Each read constructs a plugin struct; `capabilities` rebuilds an `AcquisitionCapabilities` with
2–5 `AcquisitionConfigField`s and their strings, and `isConfigured` does 2–5
`UserDefaults.standard.string` reads plus trimming. Under the house rule these run on every AppModel
publish for every visible body that touches them — and `capabilities` is a constant per plugin kind
while `isConfigured` changes only when Settings writes a field.

**Fix.** Make `capabilities` a `static let` on each plugin and have `AcquisitionManager` switch on kind
without constructing a provider. Cache the active provider as `private(set) var provider`, rebuilt in
`activePlugin.didSet` and in a new `configDidChange()` that `AppModel.setAcquisitionConfig` /
`disconnectAcquisitionPlugin` call. Cache `isConfigured` as `@Published private(set) var` recomputed at
the same two points. For `job(matchingTitle:)`, precompute a `Set<String>` of title keys per job in a
`didSet` alongside `persistJobs`.


**Verified —** Mechanics confirmed — `provider` really does construct a fresh plugin per access, and `capabilities` rebuilds a struct with 5 strings plus 2 `AcquisitionConfigField`s of 5 strings each, with no caching.

**But 5 of the 11 cited sites are not body reads.** `BrowseAlbumDetailView:1011` and `:1066` are inside async request functions; `DiscoverySearchView:2095/2096/2101` are inside `runHybridSearch(query:) async`; `ServerPlaylistViews:2244` is inside `requestMissingTrack(_:) async`. The entry also **under**-cites genuine body reads at `BrowseAlbumDetailView:48`, `ServerPlaylistViews:2226`, `DiscoverySearchView:2496–2497`, `SettingsView:194/195/223/272/460/500` and `SubscriptionsView:51`.

**Severity lowered medium → low.** What remains is a handful of small string allocations on Settings, Artist and Browse-album bodies — no scroll path, no per-row catalog scan. The fix is still correct and cheap; sell it as tidiness, not a hot path.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 25, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** PARTLY REAL · **Fix:** ADEQUATE
- **Evidence:** Mechanics confirmed: `AcquisitionManager.swift:104–109` is `var provider: AcquisitionProviding { Self.makeProvider(activePlugin) }` / `var capabilities: AcquisitionCapabilities { provider.capabilities }` / `var isConfigured: Bool { provider.isConfigured }`, and each plugin's `capabilities` builds a fresh struct literal while `isConfigured` reads `AcquisitionConfigStore.value` (`UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey:)` + trim) 2–5 times. But the cited site list is wrong in both directions. My enclosing-function trace: `BrowseAlbumDetailView:1011` is inside `private func acquisitionRequest(forPreview:) -> AcquisitionRequest`, `:1066` inside `requestAllPreviewTracksSequentially() async`, `DiscoverySearchView:2096` inside `runHybridSearch(query:) async`, `ServerPlaylistViews:2244` inside `requestMissingTrack(_:) async` — none are body reads. Genuine body-path reads it omits: `BrowseAlbumDetailView:48`, `:464` (`browseToolbarMenuExtras`), `DiscoverySearchView:1505`, `:2496`, `ServerPlaylistViews:2226` (`missingAlbumRow`), `ArtistPageView:344` (`var body`), `SettingsView:194/195/223/272/460/500`, `SubscriptionsView:51`. The cost is a handful of small string allocations and in-memory `UserDefaults` reads — no catalog scan, no per-row work, so it sits under `Rules/swiftui-body-cost.md`'s "Small things that add up" rather than the never-scan rule. Severity low is right.

The `isConfigured` cache "recomputed only in `setAcquisitionConfig` / `disconnectAcquisitionPlugin`" is the weak part: `DroppedNeedleAcquisitionPlugin.swift:278` calls `clearStoredSessionToken()` on Plex session expiry with no `AppModel` hook, and `SettingsView.swift:298` calls `app.setAcquisitionConfig(... "loginMethod")` *before* `:304` clears the token, so in both windows the cached flag would read true while the plugin's own `isConfigured` (Plex: `!storedSessionToken.isEmpty`) is false — UI enables Request, tap fails with the plugin's error. Either leave `isConfigured` a live read (it is the cheap half of this finding anyway) or, if caching, bump a revision from inside `AcquisitionConfigStore.set` / `clear` so every writer invalidates. The `job(matchingTitle:)` precompute is fine but unrelated to the body reads.

It did not examine the fix's `isConfigured` cache against the plugin-internal `sessionToken` writes; that gap is my addition, not a disagreement.

## E28 — `MyListeningView` re-summarises 500 scrobbles on every body pass, and once more per heatmap bar
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** **REINFORCED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Scrobbling/MyListeningView.swift:6–8, 135–139`

```swift
    private var summary: ListeningAnalyticsSummary {
        ListeningAnalytics.summarize(completed: app.scrobbleService.store.completed)
    }
```

```swift
    private func barHeight(for count: Int) -> CGFloat {
        let maxCount = max(summary.dailyHeatmap.map(\.playCount).max() ?? 1, 1)
        let normalized = CGFloat(count) / CGFloat(maxCount)
        return max(8, normalized * 56)
    }
```

**Problem.** Three house-rule violations at once. `summary` is a computed property referenced ~10 times
in `body` and its sections, and `barHeight` references it again for each of up to 90 bars — so one
render runs `summarize` roughly 100 times, each building dictionaries, sorting artists and tracks, and
(`ListeningAnalytics:94–98`) allocating a new `DateFormatter` and parsing every day key back into a
`Date`. The view holds `@EnvironmentObject app`, so every publish repeats all of it. The
`DateFormatter` round-trip is also gratuitous: `computeStreaks` converts dates → strings → dates to
sort days it already had as `Date`s.

**Fix.** Replace the computed property with `@State private var summary: ListeningAnalyticsSummary?`
computed in `.task` and in `.onReceive(app.scrobbleService.store.$completed)` (see **C26**), and bind
`let summary` once at the top of `body`. Pass `maxCount` into `barHeight(for:max:)` computed once in
`heatmapSection`. In `ListeningAnalytics.computeStreaks`, take `[Date]` of `calendar.startOfDay` values
instead of `Set<String>` and drop the `DateFormatter`; keep `dayKey` only for the heatmap id.

**Verified —** Both excerpts diffed byte-for-byte: identical, no abridgement. **Counted the evals myself:** 11 from `body` and its section gates (12, 21, 24, 27, 38, 39, 47, 48, 60, 80, 98) plus one per heatmap bar from `barHeight` (136), and `dailyHeatmap` is `.prefix(90)` — so the ceiling is **101 `summarize` calls per body pass**, floor 11. Two costs the entry *understates*: `barHeight` also allocates a fresh `[Int]` of the whole heatmap per bar (~8,100 extra element copies), and each `summarize` over the 500-entry store makes ~**1,090 `String(format: "%04d-%02d-%02d")` calls** plus two `localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare` sorts and the `DateFormatter` round-trip. `computeStreaks` confirmed in full, and it is worse than described — `dayKeys` is a `Set` over **all** unique days, uncapped, since `prefix(90)` applies only to the heatmap.

**Independent find — this is also a correctness bug, not only perf.** Nothing forwards `ScrobbleStore` to `AppModel` (zero hits for `store.$`, `scrobbleService.objectWillChange`, `store.objectWillChange`) and `MyListeningView` holds no `@ObservedObject` on it — so **while the screen is open a new scrobble does not refresh it**; it updates only if an unrelated AppModel publish happens to fire. That makes the proposed `.onReceive` fix a staleness fix as well as an optimisation. Same root cause as **C26**.

**Two corrections.** The "~100×" is the **ceiling stated as typical** — 90 bars needs 90 distinct days inside a 500-scrobble cap, so the real range is ~41–101. And the entry frames the cost as "every publish"; the dominant real-world cost is **screen-open latency** — the first render alone runs `summarize` up to ~100 times, a several-hundred-millisecond main-thread block before the screen paints — because the only regular publishers reaching this leaf are track changes and the throttled download sink. **Fix caveat:** `@Published` emits from `willSet`, so the `.onReceive` closure must summarise the **closure's** value, not re-read `store.completed` (still the old array at that instant); and `Published` replays on subscribe, so the extra `.task` is redundant. `ListeningAnalytics` has no other callers and no tests, so the `computeStreaks` signature change is contained to two files. Severity **medium** correct — one leaf three levels deep in Settings.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 25, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** ADEQUATE
- **Evidence:** `MyListeningView.swift:6–8` is `private var summary: ListeningAnalyticsSummary { ListeningAnalytics.summarize(completed: app.scrobbleService.store.completed) }` and my grep shows `summary` read at lines 12, 21, 24, 27, 38, 39, 47, 48, 60, 80, 98, plus `barHeight(for:)` at 135–139 re-reading `summary.dailyHeatmap` from inside the `ForEach(summary.dailyHeatmap.reversed())` at 60–64 — one `summarize` per bar, `dailyHeatmap` capped by `.prefix(90)` (`ListeningAnalytics.swift:88`). `computeStreaks` (94–98) does allocate `let formatter = DateFormatter()` per call and round-trips `dayKeys.compactMap { formatter.date(from: $0) }`. `ScrobbleStore.completed` is `@Published private(set)` with `completedCap = 500` (`ScrobbleService.swift:67, 73`). No memo, no `@State`, no equality guard anywhere on the path. Also confirmed: my grep for `store.$` / `store.objectWillChange` / `scrobbleService.objectWillChange` in `Sources/VellumMusicKit` returns no hits, so nothing forwards `ScrobbleStore` publishes to `AppModel` — the view only re-renders on unrelated `AppModel` publishes.
- **Better approach:** Direction is right (state, single bind, `maxCount` passed in, drop the `DateFormatter`). Refinements: subscribe with `.onReceive(app.scrobbleService.store.$completed) { summary = ListeningAnalytics.summarize(completed: $0) }` and summarise the closure's value — `@Published` emits from `willSet`, so re-reading `store.completed` inside the closure sees the old array; `Published` replays the current value on subscribe, so the separate `.task` is redundant. Make the `@State` non-optional with an empty default so the section gates don't all grow unwraps. Alternatively hold `@ObservedObject private var store: ScrobbleStore` and recompute in `.onChange(of: store.completed.count)` — same effect, one less publisher plumb.

## E29 — The EQ Response graph re-runs the automation engine and two `AVAudioSession` route queries on every body pass
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Equalizer/SettingsEqualizerView.swift:108–113`; `App/AppModel.swift:6231–6262`

```swift
    private var graphSection: some View {
        Section {
            EqualizerCurveGraphView(
                gains: app.effectiveEqualizerBandGains(for: app.player.activeTrack),
                comparisonGains: showsLayeredCurve ? app.equalizerBandGains : nil,
            )
```

**Problem.** `effectiveEqualizerBandGains` constructs an `EqualizerAutomationEngine`, scans
`equalizerProfiles` linearly, calls `EqualizerDeviceRoute.currentRouteKey()` **and**
`currentRouteDisplayName()` — two separate `AVAudioSession.sharedInstance().currentRoute` round-trips
to the audio server — and reads `outputVolume`, all inside `body`. Every publish re-runs it while the
EQ page is open; dragging a band publishes per tick, so the route query runs at gesture rate.
`showsLayeredCurve` and `exportPresetData` (a JSON encode) are computed properties evaluated per pass
too. And because volume is sampled only inside this function, "Loudness compensation" does not respond
to a mid-song volume change until the next track.

**Fix.** Cache the route on `AppModel` as `@Published private(set) var currentAudioRoute`, refreshed in
the existing `onAudioRouteChanged` hook (1142–1146) and at init; make
`EqualizerAutomationEngine.resolvedGains` take those strings. In the view hold
`@State private var effectiveGains: [Float]` recomputed on `.onChange` of `app.equalizerBandGains`,
`app.equalizerProfiles`, `app.player.activeTrack?.id` and the enhancement toggles. Hoist
`showsLayeredCurve` and `exportPresetData` into `let`s. For loudness, observe
`AVAudioSession.outputVolume` in `AppModel` and call `syncEqualizerToEngine()` when compensation is on.
While there, replace the `simultaneousGesture(DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0))` on the band `Slider`
(406–410) with stock `Slider(value:in:step:onEditingChanged:)` — **project memory records that
`simultaneousGesture` on a `NavigationLink` must never be used**; this is the same anti-pattern one
control over, and the stock API is built for begin/end edit sessions.


**Verified —** `body` → `graphSection` → `Section { EqualizerCurveGraphView(gains: app.effectiveEqualizerBandGains(...)) }`, and `Section`'s `@ViewBuilder content` is invoked eagerly at init, so the argument is evaluated every body pass. The two route queries confirmed independently at `EqualizerDeviceRoute.swift:9` and `:19`, both called in one expression at `AppModel:6237–6238`; `outputVolume` at 6257 sits inside the loudness branch, so "volume is sampled only inside this function" is right. `showsLayeredCurve` is read twice (112, 115); `exportPresetData` does a `JSONEncoder().encode` once per pass at 331. The `simultaneousGesture(DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0))` is at 406–410 as cited, and `setEqualizerBandGain` publishes per drag tick — so the route query really does run at gesture rate. **Scope note on the fix:** `showsLayeredCurve` and `exportPresetData` are consumed inside *sibling* section properties, so hoisting means a local `let` in each section, not one at `body` level.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 25, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Evidence:** `SettingsEqualizerView.swift:108–113` is as quoted — `gains: app.effectiveEqualizerBandGains(for: app.player.activeTrack)` inside `Section { ... }` in `graphSection`. `AppModel.swift:6231–6262` constructs `EqualizerAutomationEngine(profiles: equalizerProfiles)` and passes `routeKey: EqualizerDeviceRoute.currentRouteKey(), routeDisplayName: EqualizerDeviceRoute.currentRouteDisplayName()`; `EqualizerDeviceRoute.swift:9` and `:19` each independently evaluate `AVAudioSession.sharedInstance().currentRoute.outputs`, and `outputVolume` is read at 6257 only inside the `equalizerLoudnessCompensation` branch. `showsLayeredCurve` (131–137) is read at 112 and 115; `exportPresetData` (371–373) does `try? JSONEncoder().encode(...)` and is read at 331 inside a sibling section. The slider at 404–409 is `Slider(value: gainBinding, in: EqualizerBand.gainRange, step: 0.5).simultaneousGesture(DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0).onChanged { _ in app.beginEqualizerEditSession() } ...)`, and `setEqualizerBandGain` (6327–6335) goes through `setEqualizerBandGains`, a publish per tick. Inference about platform: `currentRoute` is an XPC round-trip to the audio server, so "at gesture rate" is the right characterisation.

## E30 — `LibrarySnapshotStore.saveAsync` is un-debounced and rewrites the entire track index on every membership mutation
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Library/LibrarySnapshotStore.swift:79–90`

```swift
    static func saveAsync(_ snapshot: LibrarySnapshot) {
        writeLock.lock()
        let generation = writeGeneration
        writeLock.unlock()
        Task.detached(priority: .utility) {
            writeLock.lock()
            let stillCurrent = generation == writeGeneration
            writeLock.unlock()
            guard stillCurrent else { return }
            save(snapshot)
        }
    }
```

**Problem.** `writeGeneration` is bumped only by `clear()`, so it protects write-after-clear but not
write-after-write. `persistLibrarySnapshot()` has 11 call sites (every album/song add/remove, every
changed poll, the track-index rebuild), and each encodes `discoveryLibraryTracks` — the whole server
track index, 10k–100k rows — plus albums and playlists, then atomically replaces the file. Add three
albums in a row and you get three multi-MB encodes racing on the utility queue; with `.atomic` the last
to *finish* wins, which is not necessarily the last to be *captured*.
`PlaylistRowsCacheStore.saveAsync` already solved this with a 2 s trailing-edge `DispatchWorkItem` and
a per-call generation bump.

**Fix.** Give `LibrarySnapshotStore.saveAsync` the same trailing debounce and per-call generation (a
shared `DebouncedJSONFileWriter<T>` would remove the duplication). Then split the snapshot into
`library-snapshot.json` (albums, playlists, membership, favorites — small, changes often) and
`library-tracks.json` (the index — large, changes rarely) so a membership edit never re-encodes the
index. Pairs with **C27**, which fixes the check-then-write window in the same two files.


**Verified —** `writeGeneration` is declared at 29, read at 63/71/81/85, and **bumped only at line 94 inside `clear()`** — confirming it protects write-after-clear but not write-after-write. `persistLibrarySnapshot` has 11 call sites, and `AppModel:1626–1635` confirms `tracks: discoveryLibraryTracks` is encoded in full on every one. The `PlaylistRowsCacheStore` precedent is exactly the shape the fix proposes: `pendingWrite?.cancel()` + `writeGeneration &+= 1` **per call** (68) + a 2 s `asyncAfter` (98). `.atomic` last-finisher-wins is a correct reading. No refutation found.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 25, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** ADEQUATE
- **Evidence:** `LibrarySnapshotStore.swift:79–90` is as quoted; `writeGeneration` is declared at 29 and the only `&+= 1` is at 94 inside `clear()`, so two `saveAsync` calls both capture the same generation, both pass `guard stillCurrent`, and both `Task.detached(priority: .utility)` encode + `data.write(to: url, options: .atomic)` concurrently — last to finish wins. `AppModel.swift:1626–1636` builds the snapshot with `tracks: discoveryLibraryTracks` on every call. My grep counts **10** `persistLibrarySnapshot()` call sites (AppModel 2323, 2478, 2902, 3193, 3337, 3364, 3376, 3384, 3551, 4561), not 11. `PlaylistRowsCacheStore.swift:65–98` is the precedent exactly as described: `pendingWrite?.cancel(); writeGeneration &+= 1` per call plus a trailing `DispatchWorkItem`. Also noted: the synchronous `save(_:)` used by `removeMetadataEntry` (161) reads but never bumps the generation, so it participates in the same race.
- **Better approach:** The trailing debounce + per-call generation bump is the right first step and should be implemented. Two things the fix omits: (1) unlike the playlist-rows cache, this snapshot is what cold launch paints the Library from, so add a synchronous flush when `scenePhase` goes to `.background` (and make `save(_:)` cancel `pendingWrite` and bump the generation so `removeMetadataEntry` can't be clobbered by a stale debounced write). (2) The `library-tracks.json` split is a persisted-schema change — `CLAUDE.md` and `PersistedModelSchema` require a migration story for `LibrarySnapshot` changes — so land it as a separate, measured change rather than bundled with the race fix; the debounce alone already collapses the "add three albums" case to one encode.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE on substance (generation bumped only in `clear()`, full-index encode per call, precedent matches). DISAGREE on one detail it repeated from the entry: the call-site count is 10, not 11, by `grep -rn "persistLibrarySnapshot("` excluding the declaration.

## E31 — Playlist-rows cache eviction is hash-ordered and contradicts its own doc; the in-memory copy has no cap
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** low · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Library/PlaylistRowsCacheStore.swift:77–87`

```swift
            var trimmed = rowsByPlaylistId
            if trimmed.count > maxPlaylists {
                // Drop empties first, then arbitrary excess — exact eviction order
                // doesn't matter since a missed entry just re-fetches on open.
                for key in trimmed.filter({ $0.value.isEmpty }).keys where trimmed.count > maxPlaylists {
                    trimmed.removeValue(forKey: key)
                }
                while trimmed.count > maxPlaylists, let key = trimmed.keys.first {
                    trimmed.removeValue(forKey: key)
                }
            }
```

**Problem.** The type doc (19–22) promises "the most-recently-written playlists win", but
`Dictionary.keys.first` is hash order — the playlist the user just opened is as likely to be evicted as
one from last month. Because the sync-ahead warm-up writes after every fetch, a user with more than 60
playlists can have the one they are looking at evicted on the very save meant to cache it. Meanwhile
`AppModel.playlistRowsCache` — the in-memory source of these writes — has no bound at all, so on a
large account it holds every playlist's `[PlaylistRowItem]` (each embedding a full `Track`) for the
session.

**Fix.** Store `touchedAt: Date` per playlist and evict oldest-first; apply the same LRU cap to the
in-memory `playlistRowsCache` in `AppModel` (bump `touchedAt` in `applyRestoredPlaylistRowsCache` and
on open). Fix the doc comment to match whichever policy ships.


**Verified —** Doc comment at 19–22 promises "the most-recently-written playlists win"; `maxPlaylists = 60`; `trimmed.keys.first` is hash order and `PlaylistRowsCache` carries no recency field — direct contradiction, confirmed. `AppModel.playlistRowsCache` has no cap and no eviction; only `removeAll()` on sign-out and per-key `removeValue`. **Correction:** "the sync-ahead warm-up writes after every fetch" is slightly strong — `fetchPlaylistRows:3735–3742` persists only when `rowId` order changed, `warmPlaylistRowsCache` caps at `prefix(40)`, and saves are debounced 2 s. Say "on first warm-up". The eviction-order bug is unaffected.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 26, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** BEST
- **Evidence:** Confirmed verbatim at `PlaylistRowsCacheStore.swift:84`: `while trimmed.count > maxPlaylists, let key = trimmed.keys.first { trimmed.removeValue(forKey: key) }` — `Dictionary.keys.first` is hash-bucket order, not insertion/write recency, contradicting the type doc's "the most-recently-written playlists win" comment (lines 19-22, verified present). Also confirmed `AppModel.playlistRowsCache` (declared `private var playlistRowsCache: [String: [PlaylistRowItem]] = [:]` at AppModel.swift:321) has no size cap anywhere — the only removals in the file are `playlistRowsCache.removeAll()` (sign-out/clear paths) and single-key `removeValue(forKey:)`, never an LRU trim.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE — prior pass's CONFIRMED verdict matches my independent read; its correction ("the sync-ahead warm-up writes after every fetch" should say "on first warm-up", since `fetchPlaylistRows` only persists on `rowId`-order change and `warmPlaylistRowsCache` caps at `prefix(40)`) is a precision nit on the problem description, not a defect in the fix.

## P16 — The hearing test applies the most boost to the bands the user hears best
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** high · **Verdict:** **REINFORCED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Equalizer/EqualizerHearingTestView.swift:92–96` (copy at 52)

```swift
    private func saveCurrentBand() {
        // Quieter tone needed → more high-frequency boost compensation.
        let compensation = (1 - toneLevel) * 10
        offsets[stepIndex] = min(max(compensation, 0), EqualizerBand.gainRange.upperBound)
    }
```

**Problem.** The user lowers the slider "until the tone is barely audible" — that slider position *is*
their hearing threshold for the band. A **low** threshold (still audible at 2%) means good sensitivity
and needs no compensation; a **high** threshold (must stay near 100% to hear it) means reduced
sensitivity and needs boost. The code inverts it: `toneLevel = 0.02` → 9.8 dB boost, `toneLevel = 1.0`
→ 0 dB. A user with ordinary age-related high-frequency loss ends up with their **low** bands boosted
and their highs untouched, and "Apply hearing profile" writes that into `equalizerHearingOffset`, which
is summed into every track played. The footer copy at line 52 was written to match the code, so it is
confidently wrong too.

Secondary defect in the same view: `stopTone()` calls
`AVAudioSession.sharedInstance().setActive(false, …)` and `activateAudioSession()` rewrites the shared
category and options with `.mixWithOthers` — both act on the app's single shared session, so closing
the test can deactivate the session under the main player and leave the engine's category options
replaced.

**Fix.** Store the raw `toneLevel` per band during the test, then on completion compute the offsets
*relative to the user's best band* so the reference is zero:
`offsets[i] = min((level[i] - minLevel) * 10, EqualizerBand.gainRange.upperBound)`, rounded to 0.5 dB.
Change the line-52 footer to "The louder you needed the tone, the more that band is boosted." For the
session: do not call `setCategory` / `setActive(false)` on the shared session — pause `app.player`
before the test and reuse the engine's existing session configuration, or at minimum read and restore
the previous category and options in `stopTone`.


**Verified —** **I tried hard to collapse this and could not.** The slider is stock and not reversed: `Slider(value: $toneLevel, in: 0.02 ... 1, step: 0.02)` (37), displayed as a percentage beside the label "Tone level" (31–33); `updateToneVolume()` sets `engine.mainMixerNode.outputVolume = toneLevel` (149–152) and the initial synthesis multiplies by `toneLevel` (126) — **higher is louder** on both paths. Each band resets to `toneLevel = 1.0` (83), consistent with the instruction at 20: *"Play the tone at full volume, then lower the slider until it is barely audible."* So the captured value **is** the threshold, and `compensation = (1 - toneLevel) * 10` inverts it. Traced the whole flow to rule out a downstream re-inversion: `applyHearingTestOffsets` → `EqualizerPreset.normalizedGains` (a pure clamp) → `equalizerHearingOffset` → `EqualizerAutomationEngine.swift:50–51` `zip(gains, hearingOffset).map { $0 + $1 }` — **additive, no sign flip anywhere**.

Steelman rejected: `toneAmplitude(for:)` (154–161) pre-scales bass 0.9 → treble 0.28, but that is a fixed per-frequency scale independent of `toneLevel`, and it makes the bug **worse** — it pushes treble thresholds toward higher `toneLevel`, which under this formula earns *less* boost. It is the exact mechanism producing the predicted outcome for age-related HF loss.

**Two further defects found.** (1) **Double volume scaling after any Stop/Play cycle:** `playTone` bakes `toneLevel` into the buffer (126) *and* sets `outputVolume = 1` (135); after a Stop/Play the buffer is rebuilt at `base × toneLevel` and the next slider move multiplies again, giving `base × toneLevel²` — so the displayed percentage stops corresponding to the actual level and the recorded threshold is not even a consistent measurement of the wrong thing. (2) **The engine's own mitigation is unreachable:** `PlaybackEngine.activateAudioSession:427` names this view explicitly (*"the hearing test left `.mixWithOthers` behind"*) and treats it as `unwanted` at 429 — but the test's `setActive(false, …)` never clears `isAudioSessionActive`, so the `guard !isAudioSessionActive else { return }` at **423** short-circuits before the repair at 430–435 can run. Also, `.mixWithOthers` (106) means the tone plays *over* whatever is still playing, which corrupts the measurement on its own.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 05, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** ADEQUATE
- **Evidence:** `saveCurrentBand()` (EqualizerHearingTestView.swift:92-96) computes `let compensation = (1 - toneLevel) * 10`. The slider goes from full volume down to "barely audible" (footer at line 20: "Play the tone at full volume, then lower the slider until it is barely audible"), and `updateToneVolume()` sets `engine.mainMixerNode.outputVolume = toneLevel` (line 151) — higher `toneLevel` is louder, so a low final `toneLevel` means the tone was still audible near-silent (good hearing, should need no boost) yet `compensation` is highest there (`toneLevel=0.02` → 9.8 dB). This is inverted from correct hearing-aid logic. Also confirmed the secondary session defect: `stopTone()` calls `AVAudioSession.sharedInstance().setActive(false, options: .notifyOthersOnDeactivation)` (line 170) and `activateAudioSession()` sets `.mixWithOthers` on the shared session (line 106).
- **Better approach:** The proposed relative-to-best-band normalization (`offsets[i] = min((level[i]-minLevel)*10, upperBound)`) is defensible audio-engineering but adds real complexity (must store every raw `toneLevel` and defer the whole offsets computation until all bands are collected, restructuring `saveCurrentBand`'s per-step assignment). A simpler, equally-correct fix that needs no restructuring: just flip the sign in place — `let compensation = toneLevel * EqualizerBand.gainRange.upperBound` (or `* 10`) — computed per-band exactly where the buggy line is today, with no cross-band bookkeeping.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE — prior pass did an exceptionally thorough problem verification ("I tried hard to collapse this and could not"), traced the additive-only downstream path to rule out re-inversion, and found two additional defects (buffer/volume double-scaling on Stop/Play cycles, and the fact that `stopTone`'s `setActive(false)` never clears `isAudioSessionActive` so `PlaybackEngine`'s own designed-for-this-view session repair at `activateAudioSession:423` never runs). None of that changes my PROBLEM verdict; it only reinforces it.

## P17 — EQ settings copy still describes the removed cache-then-swap engine, and "Stereo width" is a tone tilt
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Equalizer/SettingsEqualizerView.swift:103–105` (also 126, 275); `App/AppModel.swift:736–745`; `Equalizer/EqualizerProfileModels.swift:24–33`

```swift
        } footer: {
            Text("EQ applies to downloads and cached streams. Enabling EQ turns on stream caching — new streams play immediately and switch to EQ once cached. Internet radio always bypasses EQ.")
        }
```

**Problem.** With the tap architecture every progressive item carries the EQ from its first sample
(`TapPlayerItem.swift:14–17`), so "applies to downloads and cached streams", "switch to EQ once
cached" (104), "live streams and radio use normal playback until cached" (126) and "Use a downloaded
song to hear changes immediately" (275) are all false — a user will conclude the feature is broken on
streams. The `equalizerEnabled` `didSet` at `AppModel:739–741` still force-enables
`streamingDiskCacheEnabled`, a leftover of the old path that silently turns on a 512 MB disk cache the
user did not ask for (see **C08**). Separately `EqualizerStereoWidth` ("Mono", "Narrow", "Wide",
"Extreme") is implemented as `bandTilt` added identically to **both** channels — it does not touch
inter-channel difference at all, "Mono" does not sum L+R, and "Extreme" adds +8 dB at 16 kHz. The
label promises something the audio does not do.

**Fix.** Rewrite the three footers: 104 → "EQ applies to every track from the first note. Internet
radio is not equalized."; 126 → "Use Bypass to A/B against your curve."; 275 → drop the last sentence.
Delete `AppModel:739–741`. For stereo width, either implement it honestly in `tapProcess` — the tap
already has both channel buffers, so mid/side is `m = (L+R)/2, s = (L-R)/2 * width; L = m+s, R = m-s`
with `width` stored as one `Float` in `TapRenderState` — or rename the picker to "Tone tilt" with
Dark/Warm/Neutral/Bright/Brilliant.


**Verified —** Stereo width checked exhaustively: `grep -rn 'stereoWidth|StereoWidth'` = 12 hits, and the **only** consumer is `EqualizerAutomationEngine:42–43` → `applyStereoTilt` → line 76 `zip(normalizedGains(gains), tilt).map { $0 + $1 }`, producing a single 10-band `[Float]`. `tapProcess:488–512` reads `coefficients[setBase + band]` where `setBase` derives only from `activeCoefficientSet`, **not** `bufferIndex` — only `filterState` is per-channel. So both channels get identical filters and there is no cross-channel term anywhere in the render path. "Symmetric tilt, never touches inter-channel difference" confirmed at the DSP level. Copy claims confirmed against `TapPlayerItem.swift:14–17` and the explicit tombstones at `PlaybackEngine.swift:149–160` and `2792–2809` (*"Deliberately not replaced with anything. The absence is the fix."*). "Internet radio always bypasses EQ" is the one true clause.

**Missed instance:** `README.md:52` carries the same dead claim in user-facing docs — *"It needs a local copy of the audio to work… Caching streamed songs is off by default; turning the equalizer on enables it for you."* Add it here or to **P20**. **Fix scope:** deleting `AppModel:739–741` contradicts CLAUDE.md's stream-cache line, which must go in the same change (see the C08 addendum); and moving stereo width into `tapProcess` removes it from `effectiveEqualizerBandGains`, which also feeds `EqualizerCurveGraphView` and `showsLayeredCurve` — both need updating or the graph silently stops reflecting the control.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 26, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** BEST
- **Evidence:** `TapPlayerItem.swift:14-17` states "A tap is attached to **every** item, whether or not the equalizer is on... Attaching or detaching a tap mid-playback is audible — that is the failure this whole branch exists to remove." `PlaybackEngine.swift:151-160` explicitly tombstones the old architecture: "There used to be an `EqualizedAudioEnginePlayer`... Nothing swaps mid-track, because there is nothing to swap to." So the three footers (still reading "switch to EQ once cached" etc. at SettingsEqualizerView.swift:104/126/275) describe removed behavior. Confirmed `AppModel.swift:739-741`: `if equalizerEnabled { UserDefaults.standard.set(true, forKey: "streamingDiskCacheEnabled") }`. Confirmed stereo width is a shared mono tilt: `EqualizerAutomationEngine.swift:75-77` `private func applyStereoTilt(_ gains: [Float], tilt: [Float]) -> [Float] { zip(...).map { $0 + $1 } }` operating on one `[Float]` gains array (no L/R split), and `EqualizerProfileModels.swift:31` gives `.extreme` the tilt `[0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]` — index 9 (16 kHz) is +8 dB, exactly as claimed.

**Problem.** `ScrobbleExclusion.Kind.artist` exists and `excludeArtist(_:)` exists, and the Settings

menus" — but the only call site anywhere is `excludeAlbum` (`NowPlayingView:1276`); `excludeArtist`
and `excludePlaylist` are dead. Even if wired, `isExcluded` never checks `.artist`, and `Track` has no
artist-id field, so an exclusion keyed on `LibraryArtistSummary.id` could not match. A user who reads
the Settings copy goes looking for a control that does not exist.

**Fix.** Decide the key first: store artist exclusions by
`LibraryTrackMatcher.normalize(artist.name)` — the same key `automatedBaseGains` already uses for EQ
artist profiles (`AppModel:6296`) — since `Track` carries only the name. Add the matching clause to
`isExcluded`. Then either wire `excludeArtist` into the artist-page toolbar menu and `excludePlaylist`
into the playlist context menu (**the standard song-menu template applies — see C01**), or delete both
functions and change the Settings copy to "albums" only.


**Verified —** Dead-call-site claim verified across Sources/host/Tests: `excludeAlbum` has one caller (`NowPlayingView:1276`); `excludeArtist` and `excludePlaylist` have **zero**. `ScrobbleExclusion.Kind` does declare `.artist`, and `isExcluded` checks only `.album` and `.playlist`. Settings copy verbatim.

**One supporting claim is false, and it invalidates the recommended fix.** "`Track` has no artist-id field" is wrong — `MusicLibraryProviding.swift:267` declares `var artistId: String?`, with a doc comment saying it exists precisely because "a name is not an identity" and that both backends send it. So an exclusion keyed on `LibraryArtistSummary.id` **could** match. The real reason it is nil at scrobble time is **C10** (`withArtworkURL`/`withDuration` drop it on the playback path). **Re-scoped fix:** key artist exclusions on `Track.artistId` with a normalized-name fallback for the nil case, and land **C10** alongside — otherwise the id is nil exactly where it matters.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 26, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** PARTLY REAL · **Fix:** ADEQUATE
- **Evidence:** Confirmed real: `grep -rn "excludeArtist(" Sources` and `excludePlaylist(` return only their own definitions at `ScrobbleService.swift:224`/`228`, no call sites, while `excludeAlbum(` has exactly one caller (`NowPlayingView.swift:1276`); `isExcluded` (ScrobbleService.swift:155-163) checks only `.album` and `.playlist`. But the finding's technical premise is false: `Track has no artist-id field` is wrong — `MusicLibraryProviding.swift:267` declares `var artistId: String?` on `Track`, with a doc comment saying both backends already send it, and both backends do populate it at parse time (`JellyfinMusicClient.swift:1762 artistId: Self.jellyfinArtistItemId(dict)`, `NavidromeClient.swift:1016 artistId: navidromeCoerceString(dict["artistId"])`), which is the same id space as `LibraryArtistSummary.id`.
- **Better approach:** Key artist exclusions on `Track.artistId == exclusion.id` directly (matching `LibraryArtistSummary.id`'s id space) rather than name-normalizing via `LibraryTrackMatcher.normalize(artist.name)`; the name-based match still "works" but is strictly worse (collides on same-named different artists) when a reliable id already exists on the model. Falling back to name-normalize only makes sense if `artistId` turns out to be nil on the actual scrobble/playback code path (a separate question not evidenced in this finding).
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE — the prior pass independently flagged the exact same false premise ("`Track` has no artist-id field is wrong — `MusicLibraryProviding.swift:267` declares `var artistId: String?`") and re-scoped the fix identically, additionally tracing that `artistId` is nil at scrobble time specifically because of a different bug (`C10`, `withArtworkURL`/`withDuration` dropping it) — a deeper root-cause link I did not chase down but which is consistent with what I found.

## P19 — "Total plays" is silently capped at 500, and the completed list is re-serialised to `UserDefaults` on every scrobble
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** low · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Scrobbling/ScrobbleService.swift:73, 91–97`

```swift
    private static let completedCap = 500
    // ...
    func recordCompleted(_ item: CompletedScrobble) {
        completed.insert(item, at: 0)
        if completed.count > Self.completedCap {
            completed = Array(completed.prefix(Self.completedCap))
        }
        persistCompleted()
    }
```

**Problem.** `ListeningAnalytics.summarize` reports `totalPlays = completed.count`, so "My Listening"
shows "Total plays: 500" forever once a listener passes 500 scrobbles, and "Longest streak" / "Top
artists" quietly become "within the last 500 plays" with no label saying so. Home mixes (On Repeat /
Rediscover) read the same list, so their history window is also 500. Each insert is `insert(at: 0)` —
an O(n) shift — followed by a JSON encode of all 500 rows into `UserDefaults`, while the convention
elsewhere (`MusicSubscriptionStore`, `EqualizerProfileStore`) is a JSON file in Application Support.

**Fix.** Keep the capped list for mixes, but add persisted aggregates to `ScrobbleStore`:
`totalPlaysAllTime: Int`, `playsByDay: [String: Int]` (pruned to ~400 days) and `firstScrobbleDate`,
updated in `recordCompleted` **before** truncation; have `summarize` take those for total/streaks/
heatmap and the list only for top artists and tracks. If the aggregates are not added, change the
Overview header to "Last 500 plays". Move `pending`/`completed`/`exclusions` to
`Application Support/VellumMusic/scrobbles.json` with a one-time migration, and append rather than
insert-at-0 (sort descending on read). Pairs with **L24**.


**Verified —** Every number re-run: `completedCap = 500` enforced in `recordCompleted`, `replaceCompleted` and `mergeCompleted`; `ListeningAnalytics:22–23` is literally `let totalPlays = plays.count`; surfaced as `statRow("Total plays", …)` at `MyListeningView:38` under a `Text("Overview")` header, so the proposed header change has a real target. Streaks, top artists, top tracks and the heatmap all derive from the same capped list, and Home mixes read it too (`HomeMixBuilder:53/72/74/94`). `insert(at: 0)` + full re-encode confirmed. Convention claim confirmed: `EqualizerProfileStore` and `MusicSubscriptionStore` both use Application Support while all three scrobble stores use `UserDefaults`. **Note:** severity `low` fits the perf half, but a silent 500 cap on a headline stat *labelled* "Total plays" is a correctness/honesty problem — worth a sentence in the entry.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 26, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** BEST
- **Evidence:** Confirmed `private static let completedCap = 500` (ScrobbleService.swift:73) and `func recordCompleted(_ item: CompletedScrobble) { completed.insert(item, at: 0); if completed.count > Self.completedCap { completed = Array(completed.prefix(Self.completedCap)) }; persistCompleted() }` (lines 91-97) exactly as quoted. `ListeningAnalytics.swift:22-23` is literally `let plays = completed; let totalPlays = plays.count`, surfaced via `MyListeningView.swift:38 statRow("Total plays", value: "\(summary.totalPlays)")`. Home mixes read the same store: `HomeMixBuilder.swift` takes `completedScrobbles: [CompletedScrobble]` and `AppModel.swift:1981/4763` pass `scrobbleService.store.completed` into it. `persistCompleted()` → `Self.save` → `UserDefaults.standard.set(data, forKey:)`, confirming the UserDefaults-not-a-file claim.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE — matches prior CONFIRMED verdict and the same evidence trail (cap enforced in `recordCompleted`/`replaceCompleted`/`mergeCompleted`, convention mismatch against `EqualizerProfileStore`/`MusicSubscriptionStore`).

## C10 — `Track.withArtworkURL` / `withDuration` silently drop `artistId` on the playback path
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** high · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Backends/MusicLibraryProviding.swift:313–334` (and 336–357)

```swift
    func withArtworkURL(_ newArtworkURL: URL?) -> Track {
        Track(
            id: id,
            title: title,
            albumId: albumId,
            albumTitle: albumTitle,
            artist: artist,
            // … duration, discNumber, indexNumber, artworkURL: newArtworkURL, libraryAddedDate,
            // … genres, releaseYear, sampleRateHz, audioChannels (elided — see file)
            audioCodec: audioCodec,
            audioBitDepth: audioBitDepth,
            audioBitRateKbps: audioBitRateKbps,
            streamOverrideURL: streamOverrideURL,
        )
    }
```

**Problem.** `artistId` was added as a trailing `var` with a default in `init` (288), but neither
copy-with method passes it through, so it silently reverts to `nil`. Both sit on the playback path:
`AppModel.trackWithResolvedArtwork` (1482) and `PlaybackEngine.tracksWithResolvedArtwork` (842) rebuild
every enqueued track, and `PlaybackEngine:1291` / `OfflineDownloadManager:745, 814, 843` rebuild via
`withDuration`. `NowPlayingView` then reads `track.artistId` at 1023/1185/1550/1622 for "Go to Artist"
and gets `nil`, falling back to the by-name lookup the field was introduced to eliminate — the
"eighteen acts called Rocket" case its own doc comment (258–267) describes. Both clients parse the id
correctly (Navidrome 1016, Jellyfin 1762); it is lost in transit. This is also why **E15**'s
12,000-artist fetch fires as often as it does.

**Fix.** Replace both hand-rolled copy constructors with mutation of a copy —
`var copy = self; copy.artworkURL = newArtworkURL; return copy` — which needs the stored properties
changed from `let` to `var` (it is a value type; nothing is lost). If `let` must stay, add
`artistId: artistId` to both. Either way add a unit test that round-trips a `Track` with every field
non-nil through both methods and asserts equality except the changed field, so the next added field
cannot regress the same way.


**Verified —** Excerpt honestly marked; `artistId: String? = nil` really is the trailing init param at **288**. `grep -rn '\.artistId *=' Sources` returns exactly one hit — the init body — so nothing restores it post-construction. **Worse than described:** `AppModel.trackWithResolvedArtwork` does guard on an unchanged URL, but `PlaybackEngine.tracksWithResolvedArtwork:839–844` does **not**, and `resolveArtwork` is bound unconditionally at `AppModel:1012` — so for any track with resolvable art it rebuilds even when the URL is identical, across all four entry points (732, 783, 803, 825). **Every track entering the queue loses `artistId`**, not just ones whose artwork changed. **Additional:** `OfflineDownloadManager:745/814/843` write the stripped copy back into `record.track`, which `saveManifest` persists — so for downloaded tracks the loss is **durable on disk**, surviving relaunch and not repaired by a re-parse (no migration needed, though, since the field is optional). Fix is safe; `let` → `var` is source-compatible here.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 05, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** ADEQUATE
- **Evidence:** `var artistId: String?` is a trailing init parameter with a default (`MusicLibraryProviding.swift:288`, `artistId: String? = nil`). Both `withArtworkURL` (313-334) and `withDuration` (336-357) construct a fresh `Track(...)` through that same initializer but never pass `artistId:`, so it silently reverts to `nil` on every call. Confirmed all cited call sites: `AppModel.trackWithResolvedArtwork` (1479), `PlaybackEngine.tracksWithResolvedArtwork` (839), `PlaybackEngine.swift:1291` (`queue[currentIndex].withDuration(seconds)`), `OfflineDownloadManager.swift:745,814,843`, and `NowPlayingView.swift:1023/1185/1550/1622` all reading `track.artistId` for "Go to Artist".
- **Better approach:** The entry itself flags the caveat that its primary recommendation (mutate-a-copy) requires changing every stored property from `let` to `var`, a much wider diff than the bug needs. The safer, minimal fix is the one it lists as the fallback: just add `artistId: artistId` as an argument to the two existing hand-rolled `Track(...)` constructors inside `withArtworkURL`/`withDuration` — a two-line change with no risk to the rest of the (Codable, Hashable) struct's field mutability contract.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE — prior pass confirmed the same root cause and found the blast radius is worse than described (`PlaybackEngine.tracksWithResolvedArtwork` has no unchanged-URL guard, so every enqueued track loses `artistId`, not just ones whose artwork changed; and for offline downloads the stripped copy is persisted to disk via `saveManifest`, making the loss durable across relaunch). Prior pass called the `let`→`var` fix "safe," which I don't dispute (it would compile and work) — I separately judge it as more invasive than necessary for this specific bug.

## C11 — The Jellyfin magic-playlist read caps at 5,000 rows with no pagination, and the truncated list overwrites `librarySongIds`
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** high · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Backends/JellyfinMusicClient.swift:958–965`; consumer `App/AppModel.swift:2295–2299`

```swift
            URLQueryItem(name: "Limit", value: "5000"),
```

```swift
        let newSongIds = Set(fetch.trackIds)
        if librarySongIds != newSongIds {
            librarySongIds = newSongIds
            didMutate = true
        }
```

**Problem.** `fetchLibraryPlaylist` builds `trackIds` from `fetchPlaylistRows`, which sends a single
`Limit=5000` request with no `StartIndex` loop and no `TotalRecordCount` check. On a Jellyfin account
whose magic playlist holds more than 5,000 songs, the ~20 s auto-sync poll receives the first 5,000,
`applyMagicPlaylistFetch` sees a different set and **replaces** `librarySongIds` — songs 5001+ vanish
from "My Library" on every device, silently, with no error. Navidrome's `getPlaylist` returns all
entries, so the two backends diverge exactly where CLAUDE.md says membership must be canonical.
`fetchPlaylistRows` also requests `MediaStreams` on every row purely to seed `librarySongIds`, which is
the heaviest field in the payload.

**Fix.** Page with `StartIndex` / `Limit=1000` (the loop `allTracks` already uses at 530–545) until
`Items.count < Limit` or `StartIndex >= TotalRecordCount`; add `EnableTotalRecordCount=true`. For the
membership seed specifically, add a lightweight `fetchPlaylistTrackIds(playlistId:)` requesting
`Fields=` (nothing) and reading only `Id`. Add the same total-vs-received completeness check
`MusicBrainzService.isPassComplete` uses, and **throw rather than return a short list** when they
disagree, so the poll keeps the previous `librarySongIds`.


**Verified —** Single request, no `StartIndex`, no `EnableTotalRecordCount`, no `TotalRecordCount` read — confirmed. The only guard is `if librarySongIds != newSongIds`, a re-render guard, not a completeness guard, so a truncated fetch replaces. Navidrome's `getPlaylist` sends only `id` with no limit, so the divergence is real. The `StartIndex`/`pageSize = 1_000` precedent is at `allTracks:530–545` as cited.

**Blast radius is larger than written:** `fetchPlaylistRows` is the *only* Jellyfin playlist-row path — it also backs every user-facing playlist detail view (`AppModel:3724, 4206`) **and** `removeTracksFromServerMagicPlaylist:3407`, which maps track ids → `jellyfinEntryId` from this same truncated list. Past row 5000, removal silently no-ops. The proposed `fetchPlaylistTrackIds` shortcut must not replace the paging fix for the general row path. **Correction:** the poll is **60 s**, not ~20 s — `startLibraryMembershipAutoSync` sleeps 60 with a comment "(was 20s)". C16 has this right; C11 and CLAUDE.md are stale.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 05, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** BEST
- **Evidence:** `JellyfinMusicClient.fetchPlaylistRows` (line 954) issues one request with `URLQueryItem(name: "Limit", value: "5000")` (line 964) and no `StartIndex` loop or `TotalRecordCount`/`EnableTotalRecordCount` check — confirmed by reading the full function body. The consumer, `AppModel.applyMagicPlaylistFetch` (line 2280+), does `let newSongIds = Set(fetch.trackIds); if librarySongIds != newSongIds { librarySongIds = newSongIds; ... }` (line 2295) — a change-detection guard only, not a completeness guard, so a truncated 5000-row fetch unconditionally replaces the full set.
- **Better approach:** N/A — the paging pattern it points to already exists verbatim in the same file (`allTracks`, JellyfinMusicClient.swift:530-545, `StartIndex`/`pageSize = 1_000` loop), and "throw rather than return a short list" slots directly into the existing error-handling path at `AppModel.swift:2129-2139`, which already preserves the previous `librarySongIds`/cached playlist id on a thrown error — so the fix reuses machinery that's already correct rather than adding new logic.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE — prior pass confirmed the same mechanism and added that the blast radius is larger than stated: `fetchPlaylistRows` also backs every user-facing playlist detail view and `removeTracksFromServerMagicPlaylist` (silent no-op past row 5000), so the fix must not scope the pagination fix to only the membership-seed shortcut. Prior pass also corrected the poll cadence to 60s, not ~20s — I independently verified this: `startLibraryMembershipAutoSync` (AppModel.swift:2151-2165) sleeps `.seconds(60)` with a comment "(was 20s)".

## C12 — Navidrome sends the membership payload as a GET query string, capping the library at ~100 albums behind a stock reverse proxy
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** high · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Backends/NavidromeClient.swift:1639–1644, 1812–1814`

```swift
    /// Updates the playlist's comment field. Used to persist ``LibraryMembershipPayload``.
    func setPlaylistComment(playlistId: String, comment: String) async throws {
        _ = try await subsonicRequest(path: "updatePlaylist", query: [
            "playlistId": playlistId,
            "comment": comment,
        ])
    }
```

**Problem.** `subsonicRequest` uses `URLSession.vellum.data(from: url)` — a **GET** — so the entire
`LibraryMembershipPayload` JSON rides in the request line at roughly 80 percent-encoded bytes per
album. nginx's default `large_client_header_buffers 4 8k` returns 414 at about 8 KB (~100 albums);
Cloudflare cuts at 16 KB (~200). Past that, every `addAlbumToLibrary` / `removeAlbumFromLibrary` throws
inside `persistLibraryMembershipPayload`, the only feedback is a 1.8 s "Couldn't sync library to
server" toast, and the **album/playlist half of the library silently stops syncing across devices while
the song half keeps working** — the user sees Recently Added diverge between phone and iPad with no
explanation. Jellyfin posts a JSON body and has no such limit.
*Unverified:* the exact byte at which a given user's proxy rejects; a bare Navidrome behind Go's 1 MB
header limit will not hit it.

**Fix.** Build the request as `POST /rest/updatePlaylist.view` with
`Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and the auth + `playlistId` + `comment` fields in the
body (Navidrome and Subsonic both accept form-encoded POST on every endpoint); add a
`subsonicPostRequest(path:form:)` helper next to `subsonicRequest` and route `updatePlaylist` through
it. Independently shrink the payload in `LibraryMembershipPayload.encoded()` — epoch seconds instead of
ISO-8601, `a`/`p` keys — so the comment column stays small either way.


**Verified —** GET confirmed unambiguously: `subsonicRequest` → `buildURL` → `URLSession.vellum.data(from: url)`, no `URLRequest`, no `httpMethod`. The three `httpMethod` sites (1059, 1114, 1138) are the **native** Navidrome API, not the Subsonic `/rest/` surface. **Payload measured rather than assumed:** with `.iso8601` dates, `.sortedKeys`, and `urlQueryAllowed` escaping, 100 albums encode to **9,357 bytes with 32-char hex ids and 9,757 with UUIDs — ~94–98 bytes/album, not ~80**. So the thresholds are *optimistic*: nginx's 8 KB request-line buffer is exhausted at roughly **80–85 albums**, Cloudflare's 16 KB at **165–170**. Tighten those downward.

**The "independently shrink the payload" half is not independent and is unsafe as ordered.** Epoch seconds and `a`/`p` keys make the new payload **undecodable by any older build**, which lands in exactly the `.empty` clobber path **C15** documents. It must ship *after* C15's `.corrupt`/`.tooNew` handling and must bump `v`. Also state a minimum Navidrome version for the POST premise rather than asserting it for Subsonic generally.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 06, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** ADEQUATE
- **Evidence:** `setPlaylistComment` (NavidromeClient.swift:1639-1644) calls `subsonicRequest(path: "updatePlaylist", query: [...])`, and `subsonicRequest` (1812-1814) is `let (data, res) = try await URLSession.vellum.data(from: url)` — a plain GET with no `URLRequest`/`httpMethod` anywhere in that function. The three `httpMethod =` sites in the file (1059, 1114, 1138) are all under `// MARK: - Native (non-Subsonic) API`, not the `/rest/` Subsonic surface used for `updatePlaylist`. So the full `LibraryMembershipPayload` JSON does ride in the query string as claimed.
- **Better approach:** The GET→POST switch (`subsonicPostRequest(path:form:)`) is correct and should ship on its own. The paired "shrink the payload" change (epoch seconds, `a`/`p` keys) is not safe to ship independently: nothing reads the `v` field (confirmed for C15 — only `self.v = v` in the initializer), so an old build reading a new compact payload fails to decode and collapses to `.empty`, landing directly in C15's clobber path. Sequence it: ship POST first, ship the compact encoding only after C15's `.corrupt`/`.tooNew` decode handling exists, and bump `v` when the format changes.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE — the earlier pass's byte-count refinement (~94-98 bytes/album with real percent-encoding overhead, not ~80) and its point that the payload-shrink half of the fix is unsafe without C15 landing first are both consistent with what I verified independently (the dead `v` field, the whole-payload GET).

## C13 — Acquisition API keys, passwords and session tokens are stored in plaintext `UserDefaults`
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** high · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Acquisition/AcquisitionCore.swift:668–690`

```swift
enum AcquisitionConfigStore {
    private static func key(_ kind: AcquisitionPluginKind, _ fieldId: String) -> String {
        "acquisition.\(kind.rawValue).\(fieldId)"
    }

    static func value(_ kind: AcquisitionPluginKind, _ fieldId: String) -> String {
        let raw = UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: key(kind, fieldId)) ?? ""
        return raw.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
    }
```

**Problem.** The Lidarr API key (full admin access to the user's Lidarr), the DroppedNeedle account
**password** (kept so the plugin can re-login), and the DroppedNeedle/Plex session token all go through
this store into the app's `.plist` — included in unencrypted backups and readable by anyone with the
container. The app already has `KeychainStore` for the Navidrome/Jellyfin credentials, so the
acquisition layer is the one place secrets bypass it. `AcquisitionConfigField.Kind` already
distinguishes `.apiKey` / `.password` from `.url` / `.text`, so the routing information exists.

**Fix.** Branch on the field's `Kind` in `AcquisitionConfigStore.set/value/clear`: `.apiKey`,
`.password` and the DroppedNeedle `sessionToken` go through `KeychainStore` (make its `saveString` /
`loadString` `internal` — **C09** proposes deleting them as dead, so coordinate: keep them and fix the
`SecItemUpdate` issue instead), keyed `"acquisition.<kind>.<field>"`; everything else stays in
`UserDefaults`. Add a one-shot migration in `AcquisitionManager.init` that moves existing secret values
out and calls `removeObject`. `set` needs the `Kind`, so change the signature to
`set(_ value: String, _ kind:, field: AcquisitionConfigField)` and update the two callers in
`AppModel.setAcquisitionConfig` (5438) and `disconnectAcquisitionPlugin` (5445).


**Verified —** Verified `UserDefaults.standard` in `value`, `set` and `clear` with no keychain anywhere, and the three secrets that route through it: `LidarrAcquisitionPlugin:18` (apiKey), `DroppedNeedleAcquisitionPlugin:34` (password), `:35, 409, 414, 420` (sessionToken). `KeychainStore` is used for the server credentials, so this is genuinely the one bypass.

**Two corrections, both enlarging the fix.** (1) The caller list is wrong: `disconnectAcquisitionPlugin` calls **`clear`**, not `set`, and the other three `set` callers are inside `DroppedNeedleAcquisitionPlugin` (409/414/420), which pass a bare `"sessionToken"` string rather than an `AcquisitionConfigField` — so the proposed `set(_:_:field:)` signature will not compile against them without a second overload. (2) **`sessionToken` is not a declared `configField`**, so `AcquisitionConfigStore.clear(kind, fields: capabilities.configFields)` does not remove it — disconnecting DroppedNeedle today leaves the live session token in the plist. The migration must sweep by key, not by field list.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 06, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** ADEQUATE
- **Evidence:** `AcquisitionConfigStore` (AcquisitionCore.swift:668-690) is exactly as quoted: `UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey:)` / `.set(...)` with no Keychain involved, while `KeychainStore` (App/KeychainStore.swift) already exists for server credentials with `private static func saveString`/`loadString`. Real secrets route through it: `LidarrAcquisitionPlugin.swift:18` (`apiKey`), `DroppedNeedleAcquisitionPlugin.swift:34` (`password`) and `:35,409,414,420` (`sessionToken`).
- **Better approach:** Don't change the `set`/`value` call signature at all. `AcquisitionConfigStore` is in the same module as `AcquisitionManager` (internal is visible target-wide), so `set`/`value`/`clear` can look up the field's `Kind` internally via `AcquisitionManager.capabilities(for: kind).configFields.first(where: { $0.id == fieldId })?.kind` and branch on that — routing `.apiKey`/`.password` to Keychain with zero caller changes. This avoids the compile break the earlier pass correctly flagged: `DroppedNeedleAcquisitionPlugin.swift:409,414,420` call `AcquisitionConfigStore.set(token, .droppedNeedle, "sessionToken")` with a bare string, not an `AcquisitionConfigField`, so the proposed `set(_:_:field:)` signature genuinely won't compile against them without a second overload.
- **Versus the first pass:** DISAGREE (partially) — I agree with the earlier pass's correction #1 (wrong caller list: `disconnectAcquisitionPlugin` calls `clear` not `set`, and the real `set` callers with bare-string ids are inside `DroppedNeedleAcquisitionPlugin`). But I disagree with correction #2: I read `DroppedNeedleAcquisitionPlugin.swift:94-101` directly and `sessionToken` **is** declared in `configFields` (`AcquisitionConfigField(id: "sessionToken", kind: .apiKey, ..., required: false)`, present since commit `0cccfa5d`, 2026-07-13, per `git blame`), and `AcquisitionCapabilities.configFields` has no filtering — it's a plain stored property. So `AcquisitionConfigStore.clear(kind, fields: AcquisitionManager.capabilities(for: kind).configFields)` does iterate over and remove the `sessionToken` key today; the claim "disconnecting DroppedNeedle today leaves the live session token in the plist" does not hold up against the code as written.

## C14 — The Lyra → Vellum migration misses almost every key it was written to migrate, and never moves the data folder
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** high · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/App/LegacyLyraMigration.swift:15–31`

```swift
    static func runIfNeeded() {
        let defaults = UserDefaults.standard
        guard !defaults.bool(forKey: markerKey) else { return }
        migrateDefaults(defaults, fromPrefix: "lyra.", toPrefix: "vellum.")
        migrateDefaults(defaults, fromPrefix: "com.randll.lyra.", toPrefix: "com.randll.vellum.")
        migrateKeychainItems(accounts: ["jellyfin", "navidrome"])
        defaults.set(true, forKey: markerKey)
    }
```

**Problem.** The rename commit (`836f7f8`) renamed `LyraMusic.favoriteTrackIds`,
`LyraMusic.recentlyPlayedEntries`, `LyraMusic.playlistCreatedDates`, `lyraThemePreference`,
`lyraOfflineMode`, `lyraPendingScrobbles`, `lyraCompletedScrobbles`, `lyraScrobbleExclusions`,
`lyraEqualizer*`, `lyraWifiStreamBitRate` … — **none of which begin with `lyra.` (dot)**. The only keys
this prefix matches are the three `lyra.killMode.*`. So an upgrading user keeps kill-mode progress and
their login and loses every setting, favourite, recently-played entry, listening history, EQ config,
followed artist and acquisition job. The same commit also renamed the on-disk root from
`Application Support/LyraMusic/` (snapshot, `Downloads/` + `offline-manifest.json`, `custom-radio/`,
`stream-cache/`) and `LyraOfflineDownloads`, and **nothing moves or deletes the old tree** — all
offline downloads vanish from the app and the bytes stay on disk as an orphan the cache-clear UI cannot
see. The marker is then set, so a corrected migration will not re-run on devices that already upgraded.
`Signing.xcconfig:27` tells developers this migration "keeps all local data", which is false.

Two further defects in the same function: the marker is written even when `SecItemCopyMatching` failed
with something other than "not found" (a locked keychain at first launch after reboot returns
`errSecInteractionNotAllowed`), so the saved server login is lost permanently; and the whole type
hard-codes `UserDefaults.standard`, so the pure defaults half cannot be tested.

**Fix.** Add `migrateDefaults(fromPrefix: "LyraMusic.", toPrefix: "VellumMusic.")` and a camel-case pass
(`key.hasPrefix("lyra") && key.dropFirst(4).first?.isUppercase == true` → `"vellum" + suffix`). Add
`migrateApplicationSupportFolder()` that `moveItem`s `Application Support/LyraMusic` → `VellumMusic`
when the destination does not exist (merging `Downloads/` when it does), plus `LyraOfflineDownloads`.
**Rename the marker to `vellum.migration.lyraLocalState.v2`** so installs that already ran v1 pick up
the rest. Only write the marker when every keychain read returned `errSecSuccess` or
`errSecItemNotFound`. Change the signature to
`runIfNeeded(defaults: UserDefaults = .standard, keychain: KeychainMigrating = SystemKeychain())` and
add `Tests/VellumMusicKitTests/LegacyLyraMigrationTests.swift` covering: `lyra.x` → `vellum.x`;
`LyraMusic.x` → `VellumMusic.x`; existing destination not overwritten; second run is a no-op; marker
not set when the injected keychain reports `errSecInteractionNotAllowed`. Fix the
`Signing.xcconfig` comment. **Do this together with L24**, which is what makes the key table
enumerable in the first place.


**Verified —** **Verified by enumeration, not sampling.** Extracted every removed `lyra`/`Lyra` string literal from `git show 836f7f8 -U0` (177 unique) and classified each. The `"lyra."` pass matches **the kill-mode trio only**. The `"com.randll.lyra."` pass matches **one** UserDefaults key (`jellyfin.deviceId`) — the other four literals with that prefix are a `UTType` identifier, a Darwin notification name and two WidgetKit `kind:` strings, none of them defaults. **Migrated: 4. Missed: ~54** — roughly 44 camel-case `lyra*` (including all 16 `lyraEqualizer*`, the scrobble trio, theme, offline mode, trusted SSL hosts, home SSIDs and the full quality set) plus 10 `LyraMusic.*` (favorites, recently-played, playlist date maps, and the magic-playlist id cache). The finding is if anything too kind. Folder rename confirmed: zero `LyraMusic`/`LyraOfflineDownloads` references outside the `.bak` file, and no `migrateApplicationSupportFolder` exists. Marker and `Signing.xcconfig:27` defects both confirmed.

**The fix is wrong on the filesystem half and must be rewritten.** Resolving each directory's real domain: the snapshot, offline manifest and custom-radio are in **Application Support** ✔; **`VellumMusic/Downloads` is in `Documents/`** ✘ — and that is the *only* thing users actually lose; `stream-cache`, `ArtworkCache` and `AccountAvatar` are in **Caches** (self-healing, low stakes); and `VellumOfflineDownloads` is in `temporaryDirectory` holding in-flight `.part` files — pointless to migrate, drop it. An Application-Support-only move would appear to fix the problem while not recovering the audio. Enumerate all three domains. The marker-rename-to-v2 approach is safe: `migrateDefaults` already skips keys whose destination exists, so a re-run cannot overwrite post-upgrade values.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 06, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** ADEQUATE
- **Evidence:** `LegacyLyraMigration.swift:15-31` matches the quote exactly. Current UserDefaults keys use `"VellumMusic.favoriteTrackIds"` / `"VellumMusic.recentlyPlayedEntries"` (AppModel.swift:343,393) and bare camelCase like `"vellumThemePreference"`, `"vellumWifiStreamBitRate"`, `"vellumEqualizerBandGains"` (AppModel.swift:484-510, EqualizerSettings.swift:50-67) — none of which begin with lowercase `"lyra."`, so `migrateDefaults(fromPrefix: "lyra.", toPrefix: "vellum.")` cannot match them; only `grep -rn "\"lyra" Sources/VellumMusicKit` still finds is the migration's own literal. `grep -rln "LyraMusic" Sources/VellumMusicKit` returns zero hits, confirming no folder-migration code exists anywhere.
- **Better approach:** The camelCase-pass and marker-versioning ideas are sound and directly verified against real key names. But the filesystem half is wrong as scoped: `OfflineDownloadManager.downloadsFolder()` (line 225-227) resolves under `.documentDirectory`, not Application Support — `VellumMusic/Downloads` (the actual audio bytes users lose) lives in **Documents**, while `StreamingMediaDiskCache`/`ArtworkURLCache` live in `.cachesDirectory` (self-healing, low stakes) and the in-flight `.part` files live under `temporaryDirectory` (pointless to migrate). A single `migrateApplicationSupportFolder()` as proposed would move the snapshot/manifest/custom-radio tree but silently leave the actual downloaded audio behind, looking fixed while it isn't. Enumerate and migrate per real domain: Application Support (snapshot, offline manifest, custom-radio), Documents (`VellumMusic/Downloads` → new downloads root), skip Caches and the tmp folder.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE — I independently confirmed `downloadsFolder()` uses `.documentDirectory` (OfflineDownloadManager.swift:225-227) and that Caches-based stores (`StreamingMediaDiskCache.swift:28`, `ArtworkURLCache.swift:125`) are separate from Application Support (`AccountAvatarCache.swift:96`), which validates the earlier pass's per-domain correction to the fix.

## C15 — A malformed, truncated or newer-version membership payload decodes to `.empty`, and the next add overwrites the server with it
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** high · **Verdict:** **REINFORCED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Library/LibraryMembership.swift:163–171` (and `v` at 151–157)

```swift
    /// Tolerant decode — an absent or malformed comment field becomes an empty payload
    /// rather than blocking sign-in. Callers re-encode and write a clean payload on the
    /// next mutation.
    static func decode(_ raw: String?) -> LibraryMembershipPayload {
        guard let raw, !raw.isEmpty, let data = raw.data(using: .utf8) else { return .empty }
        let decoder = JSONDecoder()
        decoder.dateDecodingStrategy = .iso8601
        return (try? decoder.decode(LibraryMembershipPayload.self, from: data)) ?? .empty
    }
```

**Problem.** "absent", "garbled", "truncated by the server" (see **C12**) and "written by a newer
client with `v: 2`" all collapse to the same value as "user has no albums".
`AppModel.applyMagicPlaylistFetch` (2305–2315) protects only the case where *this device* already holds
entries in memory; a fresh install, a device after "Clear metadata cache", or a second device that has
never synced reads `.empty`, shows an empty Recently Added, and the next `addAlbumToLibrary` runs
`persistLibraryMembershipPayload()` with `albums: [thatOneAlbum]` — **deleting every other album's
membership and add-date on the server**, and via the poll on every other device. The `v` field is
documented as the forward-compat mechanism but nothing reads it (`grep` finds no consumer), so an older
build reading a newer payload is exactly the clobber case. `.iso8601` without `.withFractionalSeconds`
also fails the whole decode on any date with millis.

**Fix.** Make `decode` distinguish outcomes: `.absent` (nil/blank → `.empty`), `.corrupt` (non-empty
but unparseable), `.tooNew` (`v > supportedVersion`), `.ok(payload)`. In `applyMagicPlaylistFetch`, on
`.corrupt`/`.tooNew` set `membershipPayloadIsUntrusted = true` and skip the entries update regardless
of `trackIds`; `persistLibraryMembershipPayload` must **refuse to write** while that flag is set (log +
a persistent `errorMessage`, not a toast), clearing it on the first clean parse. Use an
`ISO8601DateFormatter` with `[.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds]` fallback. Add
`Tests/VellumMusicKitTests/LibraryMembershipPayloadTests.swift`: round-trip preserves ids, order and
dates; `encoded()` is byte-identical for equal payloads; `decode(nil)`, `decode("")`, `decode("{")` and
`decode("{\"v\":2,\"albums\":[]}")` each produce the intended outcome; a truncated string causes **no
write**; `upsertAlbum` is idempotent and keeps the original `added` date.


**Verified —** `v` is confirmed dead — the only reference is `self.v = v` in the init. All four failure modes collapse to `.empty`, and a `v: 2` payload decodes *successfully* into a v1-shaped struct, so `.tooNew` is not even detectable today. The clobber reaches the server: `addAlbumToLibrary` appends to the emptied array and `persistLibraryMembershipPayload` writes a whole-list replace. `LibraryMembershipTests.swift` is confirmed 100% naming/hashing — no payload round-trip test exists.

**Two corrections.** (1) **The guard is misdescribed.** The real condition (2305–2306) tests the **fetched payload**, not local state: `let payloadHasContent = !payload.albums.isEmpty || !payload.playlists.isEmpty; if payloadHasContent || fetch.trackIds.isEmpty`. The *effect* matches the entry's description, so the conclusion survives — but the fix must target the real predicate. (2) **The fractional-seconds hazard is theoretical here, not live:** `encoded()` uses `.iso8601`, which never emits milliseconds, so no payload this app writes can trip its own decoder. Mark it *Unverified* like C12's proxy threshold; the hardening is still worth doing as a prerequisite for any other writer.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 06, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** BEST
- **Evidence:** `LibraryMembershipPayload.decode` (LibraryMembership.swift:166-171) is `(try? decoder.decode(...)) ?? .empty` — any absent, corrupt, or forward-incompatible comment collapses to the same `.empty` value. `grep -rn "\.v\b" Sources/VellumMusicKit/Library/*.swift Sources/VellumMusicKit/App/AppModel.swift` finds only `self.v = v` in the initializer — nothing reads it, so a `v: 2` payload isn't even detected, it just decodes into the v1 shape. `applyMagicPlaylistFetch`'s actual guard (AppModel.swift:2305-2306) is `let payloadHasContent = !payload.albums.isEmpty || !payload.playlists.isEmpty; if payloadHasContent || fetch.trackIds.isEmpty { ... }` — it tests the fetched payload/song-list, not "whether this device already holds entries," but the practical effect (a device with no prior in-memory entries, or one whose songs list happens to be non-empty from other devices, sees the corrupt read pass silently) matches the finding's described outcome, and `persistLibraryMembershipPayload` (2483-2499) is confirmed to be a blind whole-list replace built purely from local `libraryAlbumEntries`/`libraryPlaylistEntries`.
- **Better approach:** N/A — the `.absent`/`.corrupt`/`.tooNew`/`.ok` split plus a `membershipPayloadIsUntrusted` gate on writes is the right shape and matches the codebase's existing "don't clobber on ambiguous state" pattern already used in `refreshLibraryMembership`'s catch block.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE — the earlier pass's two corrections are accurate and match what I read myself: the guard's real predicate is on the fetched payload/trackIds, not local state (though the conclusion survives), and `encoded()` uses plain `.iso8601` (never emits fractional seconds), so the millis-decode hazard is currently theoretical for this app's own writer, not a live bug today.
