## C30 — `cachedItems` claims an album is downloaded before a byte lands, and cancelling leaves a phantom
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** high _(was medium)_ · **Verdict:** **REINFORCED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Offline/OfflineDownloadManager+Queue.swift:50–65` (with 177–186)

```swift
        let tracksToFetch = topUp ? missing : tracks
        upsertCachedItem(
            itemId: itemId,
            kind: .album,
            name: album.title,
            trackIds: tracks.map(\.id),
        )
        appendQueueItem(
            kind: .album,
            itemId: itemId,
            name: album.title,
            tracks: tracksToFetch,
        )
```

**Problem.** The manifest's `cachedItems[albumId]` is written with the **full** `trackIds` list at
*enqueue* time, and `cancelQueueItem` removes only the queue item. So "Downloaded Items" shows "12
tracks · Album" for an album with zero files, and `referenceCount(for:)` returns ≥ 1 for tracks never
downloaded. The inverse hazard is worse: a track downloaded individually via `enqueueTrack` — which
never calls `upsertCachedItem` — has refcount 0, so `removeCachedItem` on any album containing it
**deletes the file the user explicitly asked for**. The manifest is supposed to describe what is on
disk; here it describes intent.

**Fix.** Move `upsertCachedItem` out of `enqueueAlbum`/`Playlist`/`Favorites` and into
`finalizeQueueItemIfDrained`: when an item settles, write `cachedItems[item.itemId]` with
`trackIds = Array(item.completedTrackIds)` — only what actually landed — and in `cancelQueueItem`
remove `cachedItems[item.itemId]` when `completedTrackIds.isEmpty`. Have `enqueueTrack` register a
`.track` cached item on completion so refcounting covers single downloads.
`OfflineCacheBrowserView` should then count `trackIds.filter { localFile(for:) != nil }`.


**Verified —** Enqueue-time write confirmed at line **54**, before `appendQueueItem` at 59 and before a byte is fetched, and it also fires from the early-return at 42; same pattern in playlist and favorites paths. `cancelQueueItem` never touches `cachedItems`. The phantom is rendered literally at `DownloadQueueView.swift:127`.

**The refcount half is real and was traced end to end.** `enqueueTrack` calls only `appendQueueItem` — `grep -rn upsertCachedItem` returns six call sites, all album/playlist/favorites — so nothing ever registers a `.track` cached item. `referenceCount(for:payload:)` counts **only** `cachedItems.values`. Kill sequence: (1) user downloads track T alone → no `cachedItems` entry; (2) user downloads album A containing T — `enqueueAlbum`'s `missing` filter correctly skips re-fetching T, but `upsertCachedItem` uses the **unfiltered** `tracks.map(\.id)`, so T lands in `cachedItems[A].trackIds`; (3) user removes album A → `removeCachedItem` computes `referenceCount` against the already-mutated payload → **0** for T → `removeExistingDownload(for: T)`. The user's explicitly-requested file is deleted with no record they ever asked for it.

**Severity raised medium → high**, because the app puts the broken guarantee in writing: the confirmation alert at `DownloadQueueView.swift:157` reads *"Tracks shared with other downloads are kept until nothing references them."* That is a direct promise of exactly the behaviour that does not hold for individually-downloaded tracks — the only case where a user would rely on it. This is silent deletion of user-requested files behind a dialog assuring them it will not happen. The `enqueueTrack` clause of the fix is load-bearing, not optional.

**Unresolved disagreement between two agents — do not treat this entry as settled without a
tiebreak.** Round 3's user-facing-copy reviewer independently examined this same dialog string and
listed it as *checking out* — it reported "Tracks shared with other downloads are kept until nothing
references them" as honoured by `removeCachedItem`'s reference count. That directly contradicts the
verification above.

They were most likely looking at different cases: the copy reviewer at the **album-shared** case (a
track listed in two `cachedItems` entries, where the refcount does work), the verifier at the
**individually-downloaded** case (`enqueueTrack` registers no `cachedItems` entry at all, so the
refcount is 0). If the verifier is right, the copy is false exactly where a user would rely on it and
`high` stands; if the copy reviewer is right, C30 reduces to the phantom-entry half and drops back to
`medium`.

**Before implementing, settle it:** read `enqueueTrack` (`+Queue.swift:124–131`) and check whether any
path registers a `.track` cached item. The verifier reported `grep -rn "upsertCachedItem"` returning
six call sites, all inside `enqueueAlbum` / `enqueuePlaylist` / `enqueueFavorites`. If that reproduces,
the verifier is right.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 08, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** ADEQUATE
- **Evidence:** `enqueueAlbum` writes the manifest with the unfiltered full track list before any download happens: `upsertCachedItem(itemId: itemId, kind: .album, name: album.title, trackIds: tracks.map(\.id),)` runs immediately, then `appendQueueItem(... tracks: tracksToFetch,)` (only `tracksToFetch`/`missing` actually get queued). `cancelQueueItem` (lines 177-186) only does `items.remove(at: idx)` after cancelling downloads — it never touches `cachedItems`. `enqueueTrack` (124-131) calls only `appendQueueItem`, never `upsertCachedItem`, so a `grep -rn upsertCachedItem` shows all 6 call sites inside `enqueueAlbum`/`enqueuePlaylist`/`enqueueFavorites`. `removeCachedItem` then computes `referenceCount(for: trackId, payload: payload)` against the already-mutated payload and calls `removeExistingDownload(for: trackId)` when it hits 0 — so a track downloaded solo via `enqueueTrack`, later swept into an album's `cachedItems[itemId].trackIds`, gets deleted when that album is removed.
- **Better approach:** The proposed rewrite ("write `cachedItems[item.itemId]` with `trackIds = Array(item.completedTrackIds)`") drops the `topUp` case: when `enqueueAlbum` only fetches the `missing` subset because some tracks were already downloaded, `item.tracks`/`completedTrackIds` for that queue item won't include the tracks that were already present, so a straight overwrite would shrink the album's registered `trackIds` and silently un-track those pre-existing files (they'd stop being covered by the album's refcount going forward). The write in `finalizeQueueItemIfDrained` (or its caller) should instead union `item.completedTrackIds` with the pre-existing `cachedItems[item.itemId]?.trackIds` (if a record already exists from a prior download pass) rather than replacing wholesale.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE — CODE_SWEEP's verify pass traced the identical kill sequence (download track T standalone → download album A containing T → remove A → T's file deleted) and raised severity based on the `DownloadQueueView.swift:157` "kept until nothing references them" dialog promise, which I did not check but does not change my read of the underlying defect.

## C31 — A followed artist's failed request is marked "Requested" forever and never retried
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Subscriptions/MusicSubscriptionEngine.swift:142–152`

```swift
            let result = await env.enqueue(request)
            switch result {
            case .started, .alreadyActive:
                requested.insert(release.id)
                statuses.append(.init(id: release.id, title: release.title,
                                      year: release.releaseYear, coverURL: release.artworkURL, state: .requested))
            case .notConfigured, .failed:
                statuses.append(.init(id: release.id, title: release.title,
                                      year: release.releaseYear, coverURL: release.artworkURL, state: .pending))
            }
```

**Problem.** `requestedReleaseIds` is written the moment `enqueue` returns `.started` and is persisted.
**Nothing ever removes an id** — `AppModel.handleAcquisitionJobFinished` (3100–3106) only toasts on
`.failed`, and grep confirms no other writer exists. So when Lidarr later reports `.notFound` (the
indexer had nothing) or `.failed` (import failed), the next `check()` sees the id in `requested`, skips
it, and the Following page shows "Requested" indefinitely while the album is neither on the server nor
in flight. The completeness pass therefore converges to a **permanent false positive** after the first
failure per release — precisely the state the engine exists to eliminate.

**Fix.** Add `markRequestUnresolved(releaseGroupMBID:)` to `MusicSubscriptionEngine` that removes the
id from every `followed[*].requestedReleaseIds` and persists. In
`AppModel.handleAcquisitionJobFinished`, on `.failed` / `.notFound`, resolve the release-group id
(carry `releaseGroupMBID` on `AcquisitionJob` — it is on the request at enqueue time,
`AcquisitionManager.enqueue:276`) and call it. Store `requestedAt: [String: Date]` instead of a bare
`Set` so `check()` can retry anything older than N days even when the completion hook was missed (app
killed mid-download).


**Verified —** `grep -rn requestedReleaseIds` returns exactly five hits: three in the model (declaration, init param, init body) and two in the engine — the read at 102 and the write-back at 156. Between them the only mutation is `requested.insert(release.id)` at 145. **The set is monotonically non-decreasing by construction** — no `remove`, no `subtract`, no filter anywhere in the module. The skip at 122–126 is checked after the `.have` test, so a release that does eventually land still flips to `.have`; the permanent false positive is scoped precisely to "requested, failed, never arrived". `handleAcquisitionJobFinished`'s guard writes nothing back to subscriptions. The only removal path is `unfollow(id:)`, which drops the whole artist — unfollow-and-refollow is the sole escape hatch, and nothing tells the user.

**Added:** `AcquisitionJobStatus` defines `.notFound` as a distinct terminal state, and the guard drops it with **not even a toast** (only `.failed` gets one), so the headline case is silent end to end. **Two fix-safety notes:** `AcquisitionJob` genuinely has no `releaseGroupMBID`, so carrying it is required, not optional — and `requestedReleaseIds` is keyed on `release.id` (a plugin-assigned opaque string, a Lidarr album id for Lidarr), **not** the MBID, so carrying the MBID alone is insufficient; the fix needs an explicit id↔MBID mapping or it will match nothing.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 27, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** WRONG
- **Evidence:** In `MusicSubscriptionEngine.check`, `requested.insert(release.id)` (line 145) only happens on `.started`/`.alreadyActive`; `.notConfigured`/`.failed` fall through to `state: .pending` with no removal from `requested`. Grep confirms `requestedReleaseIds` is only ever read (line 102) and written back whole (`followed[idx].requestedReleaseIds = requested`, line 156) — no `remove`/`subtract`/filter anywhere. `AppModel.handleAcquisitionJobFinished` (line 3100): `guard job.status == .done else { if job.status == .failed { showTransientToast("Download failed") }; return }` — `.notFound` (a real, distinct terminal case in `AcquisitionJobStatus`) hits this same early return with not even a toast, and neither branch touches `subscriptions`.
- **Better approach:** The fix as written cannot actually unmark anything even if implemented literally, for two compounding reasons I verified independently: (1) `AcquisitionJob` genuinely has no `releaseGroupMBID` field, and the only construction site named (`AcquisitionManager.enqueue:276`) is one of at least 9 — `AcquisitionManager.swift` alone builds `resolved`/`merged` `AcquisitionJob` values at lines 463, 502, and 555 (via `applyBackendStates`/`reconcile`/`noteAbsentFromQueue`, which is the actual lifecycle path most `.failed`/`.notFound` jobs go through), and none of those copies extra fields the way it copies `title`/`artist`/`nativeId` — so a naively-added `releaseGroupMBID: String? = nil` default parameter would silently be `nil` by the time `finish()` calls `onJobFinished?(job)` in the common case. (2) Even with the id fixed, `requested`/`requestedReleaseIds` is keyed by `release.id` (`AcquisitionRelease.id`, a plugin-native/opaque id) — a field distinct from `AcquisitionRelease.releaseGroupMBID` in the same struct — so calling `markRequestUnresolved(releaseGroupMBID:)` against a set keyed by a different identifier would find no match and remove nothing without an explicit id↔MBID mapping. Needs: thread the field through every terminal-producing construction site in `AcquisitionManager.swift`, and either key `requestedReleaseIds` by MBID from the start or build/carry an id↔MBID lookup for the removal call.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE — CODE_SWEEP's Verified block independently reaches the same two-part conclusion nearly verbatim ("`AcquisitionJob` genuinely has no `releaseGroupMBID`, so carrying it is required, not optional" and "`requestedReleaseIds` is keyed on `release.id`... not the MBID... the fix needs an explicit id↔MBID mapping or it will match nothing"), confirming both defects in the proposed fix that I found by reading the construction sites and struct definitions myself.

## C32 — `subsonicRequest` discards the Subsonic error code, so auth-vs-unreachable is decided by string-matching
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Backends/NavidromeClient.swift:1822–1825`; consumer 1721–1741

```swift
        if let err = sub["error"] as? [String: Any],
           let message = err["message"] as? String {
            throw NSError(domain: "Navidrome", code: 0, userInfo: [NSLocalizedDescriptionKey: message])
        }
```

```swift
        } catch let nsError as NSError where nsError.domain == "Navidrome" {
            let msg = nsError.localizedDescription.lowercased()
            if msg.contains("wrong username") || msg.contains("password")
                || msg.contains("not authorized") || msg.contains("token authentication") {
                return .authRejected
            }
            return .unreachable
```

**Problem.** Subsonic's `error.code` is the contract (40 wrong credentials, 41 token auth unsupported,
50 not authorized, 70 not found); Navidrome's message strings are not — they are localisable and have
changed between releases. `probeAuthStatus` therefore decides whether to re-POST the user's password
from a `contains("password")` test, and every other caller gets an `NSError` with `code: 0` that cannot
distinguish "playlist not found" from "session expired". Lines 1725–1729
(`if let err = items["error"]`) are unreachable — `subsonicRequest` has already thrown. A Subsonic
error whose `message` is missing is swallowed entirely and the caller parses the error envelope as a
success payload. Same class of defect as **C23**.

**Fix.** Add `case subsonic(code: Int, message: String)` to `NavidromeClientError`, throw it whenever
`sub["error"]` exists (defaulting the message to `"Subsonic error \(code)"`), and rewrite
`probeAuthStatus` as `catch NavidromeClientError.subsonic(let code, _) where code == 40 || code == 41
|| code == 50 { return .authRejected }`. Delete the dead `items["error"]` branch. Add
`var isAuthFailure: Bool` so `AppModel` can route session-expired uniformly for both backends.


**Verified —** The discard is real: `subsonicRequest` throws `code: 0` carrying only `err["message"]`, and `err["code"]` — the Subsonic contract — is read nowhere. `probeAuthStatus` is confirmed the *only* consumer that inspects a Navidrome-domain error, so every other caller gets `code: 0` and cannot separate "not found" (70) from "session expired" (40/41/50).

**One claim refuted: "lines 1725–1729 are unreachable" is wrong on both counts.** The range is off (1725 is the `status == "ok"` return; the error branch is 1726–1729), and **the branch is reachable**: `subsonicRequest` throws only when `sub["error"]` exists **and** `err["message"]` is a `String`. An error carrying a `code` but no `message` does not throw — the envelope is returned as `sub`, and `items["error"]` is live. It is in fact the only path on which the correct code-based check ever executes. The entry contradicts itself two sentences later. So **"delete the dead branch" is unsafe standalone** — it is only safe once `subsonicRequest` throws on *any* `sub["error"]`, which the same fix specifies; sequence them or state the dependency.

**Missed second site:** the identical swallow is duplicated at **`NavidromeClient.swift:128–131`** in the album-list path. Any fix must touch both. **Compile note:** `NavidromeClientError` has an exhaustive `switch self` in `errorDescription`, so adding a case without an arm is a compile error.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 28, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** ADEQUATE
- **Evidence:** `subsonicRequest` (NavidromeClient.swift:1822-1825) does exactly what's claimed: `if let err = sub["error"] as? [String: Any], let message = err["message"] as? String { throw NSError(domain: "Navidrome", code: 0, ...) }` — the Subsonic `error.code` is never read, and `probeAuthStatus` (line ~1727) string-matches `nsError.localizedDescription.lowercased()` for "password"/"not authorized"/etc. I also confirmed the "unreachable" claim about lines 1725-1729 is itself wrong: if `err["message"]` is missing (only `code` present), `subsonicRequest` does NOT throw, so `sub` is returned intact and `probeAuthStatus`'s `if let err = items["error"]` branch (which does check the numeric code) is the live path — it isn't dead code in general, only in the common case where a message is present.
- **Better approach:** The identical error-swallowing pattern is duplicated verbatim at `NavidromeClient.swift:127-131` inside `fetchAlbumList2Page` (`if let err = sub["error"] as? [String: Any], let message = err["message"] as? String { throw NSError(domain: "Navidrome", code: 0, ...) }` — same bug, separate code path that doesn't go through `subsonicRequest`). The fix as written only touches `subsonicRequest`/`probeAuthStatus` and would leave this second site swallowing codes exactly as before. Fix both through one shared error-parsing helper, and sequence "make `subsonicRequest` throw on any `sub["error"]`" before "delete the dead `items["error"]` branch" since the latter is only safe after the former.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE — the recorded verdict independently reaches the same two conclusions I did before reading it: the "unreachable" framing is self-contradicting/wrong, and the fix misses the duplicate swallow at line ~128-131.

## C33 — Jellyfin list endpoints ignore the HTTP status, so a 401/403/500 reads as an empty catalog
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** **REINFORCED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Backends/JellyfinMusicClient.swift:349–354` (same at 449, 470, 503, 522, 563); 1181–1184

```swift
        var req = URLRequest(url: comps.url!)
        applyAuth(&req)
        let (data, _) = try await URLSession.vellum.data(for: req)
        let json = try JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: data) as? [String: Any]
        let items = json?["Items"] as? [[String: Any]] ?? []
        return items.compactMap(parseAlbum)
```

**Problem.** `albums(limit:)`, `recentlyAdded`, `recentlyPlayed`, `albums(forLibraryArtistId:)`,
`tracks(forLibraryArtistId:)`, `albums(inGenre:)`, `tracks(forAlbumId:)` and `fetchAudioItemsPage` all
discard the response. A 403 with a JSON body decodes to a dict without `Items` and returns `[]` — the
app then believes the server has **zero albums** and repaints Home and Library empty, and
`handleAcquisitionJobFinished`'s "retry `searchCatalog` until the file surfaces" loop spins against a
server that is refusing it. `searchCatalog` goes further, converting every failure to `.empty`, whereas
Navidrome's throws — so feature code (six `(try? await lib.searchCatalog(...)) ?? .empty` sites) cannot
tell "no match" from "down" on either backend. Other methods in the same file (`libraryArtists` 374,
`fetchPlaylistSummaries` 946) do check status, so this is inconsistency, not policy.

**Fix.** Add one private helper `itemsRequest(_ url: URL, query: [URLQueryItem]) async throws ->
[[String: Any]]` that builds the request, applies auth, throws
`JellyfinClientError.badResponse(status:message:)` via `humanReadableError` on non-2xx, and returns
`Items`. Route all ~20 hand-rolled copies through it (this also removes the duplicated
`albumId = AlbumId ?? ParentId` closure at 475, 568, 914, 1203, 1267). In `searchCatalog`, keep partial
results but rethrow when all three subtasks fail, and add `var isPartial: Bool` to
`CatalogSearchResults` so callers can say "some results unavailable". **E26**'s fix depends on this
helper.


**Verified —** Enumerated all 31 `URLSession.vellum.data(for: req)` calls in the file: exactly **six** bind `(data, _)` and drop the response — lines 351, 451, 472, 505, 524, 565 — and each was resolved to its enclosing function. Eight named methods against six sites reconciles correctly, because `albums(limit:)`, `recentlyAdded` and `recentlyPlayed` all funnel through `fetchAlbumSummaries`. The other 25 guard properly, and the two counter-examples are real at ±1 from the cited lines — so "inconsistency, not policy" is right (6 of 31). `searchCatalog` verified in both clients: Jellyfin collapses all three subtasks with `(try? await …) ?? []`; Navidrome propagates. The entry's "a 403 **with a JSON body**" hedge is the right one — a bare or HTML body throws at `JSONSerialization` — and ASP.NET `ProblemDetails` is such an object, so the case is live.

**The empty result is written to disk.** `refreshLibraryAlbums` sets `libraryAlbumsLoadError = nil` at 3532, assigns `libraryAlbums = fetched + preserved` at 3547 with **no non-empty guard**, and calls `persistLibrarySnapshot()` at 3551. So a single 403 does not just blank the session — it **persists the blank catalog**, where it survives relaunch until a successful fetch replaces it, and because nothing threw the UI presents a confidently empty library rather than a failure state. **Minor:** there are **seven** `(try? await lib.searchCatalog(…)) ?? .empty` sites, not six (six in `AppModel`, plus `DiscoverySearchView:2105`). Fix compiles — `badResponse(status:message:)` and `humanReadableError(from:)` already exist, and `CatalogSearchResults` uses the memberwise init so a defaulted `isPartial` keeps every call site compiling.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 28, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

[[String: Any]] ?? []` with no status check, while `libraryArtists` (line ~373) and `fetchPlaylistSummaries` (line ~940) do `guard let http = res as? HTTPURLResponse, http.statusCode == 200 else { throw URLError(.badServerResponse) }`. `searchCatalog` (1171-1184) does `let songs = (try? await songsTask) ?? []` for all three subtasks, silently converting any failure — including a thrown non-2xx from the underlying `searchAudioItems`/`searchAlbumItems`/`searchArtistItems`, which do check status — into an empty result.
- **Better approach:** N/A — verified `JellyfinClientError.badResponse(status:message:)` and `humanReadableError(from:)` already exist in the file, and `CatalogSearchResults`'s memberwise init means a defaulted `isPartial` won't break `static let empty`. I also checked `refreshLibraryAlbums` (AppModel.swift:3530-3570): it does `let fetched = try await all` with no `try?`, so once `albums(limit:)` actually throws on a bad status instead of returning `[]`, the catch block at 3567 fires and calls `restoreLibraryFromDisk()` instead of persisting an empty catalog — this fix incidentally also closes that "persists the blank catalog" hole.

## C34 — One failed `getSong` aborts the whole playlist or favorites load on Navidrome
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** low _(was medium)_ · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Backends/NavidromeClient.swift:910–927`

```swift
            try await withThrowingTaskGroup(of: Track?.self) { group in
                for id in chunk {
                    group.addTask { try await self.fetchTrackViaGetSong(id: id) }
                }
                for try await track in group {
                    if let track { tracks.append(track) }
                }
            }
```

**Problem.** This is the path for minimal-payload rows in `fetchPlaylistRows` (1225) and
`fetchFavoriteTracks` (792). A single `getSong` that 404s — a track deleted since the playlist was
built, the exact stale-id situation **C17** exists for — or times out on a flaky link throws out of the
group, and the **entire playlist fails to load**, discarding the hundreds of rows already parsed. The
sibling `expandFavoriteAlbumTracks` (816–840) uses `withTaskGroup` + `try?` and degrades gracefully;
the two were written to different policies.

**Fix.** Switch to `withTaskGroup(of: (String, Track?).self)`, capture the error per id, and return
`(tracks, failedIds)`. In `fetchPlaylistRows`, keep the failed row with a placeholder `Track` built
from whatever the entry dict had (id + `titleFromPath`) so index positions stay correct — **a dropped
row shifts every later `navidromeIndex` and makes the batched removal at 1354–1368 delete the wrong
songs**, which is a destructive consequence, not a cosmetic one. Throw only if every id in the batch
failed.


**Verified —** What holds: the `withThrowingTaskGroup` + `for try await` really does let one throwing child kill the group, `subsonicRequest` really turns a Subsonic error-70 (HTTP 200) into a throw rather than a nil, and both callers use plain `try await`. Reachability of the minimal-payload path confirmed — `parseSongFromChildDict` has two `return nil` sites and **953 (missing `albumId`) is exactly the minimal-payload case**, so the `getSong` path is genuinely live. The `expandFavoriteAlbumTracks` policy contrast is accurate.

**The destructive half is refuted, and it was the reason for the severity.** `navidromeIndex` is **not** the compacted output position — it is `pair.idx` from `for (idx, dict) in entries.enumerated()` over the **raw server entry array** (1215), carried through and emitted at 1238; the native path does the same (1257–1263). A dropped row leaves a hole and **every surviving row keeps its correct server index**. Both removal call sites consume `row.navidromeIndex`, never an array position (`AppModel:3415–3418`, `4145–4160`). So a dropped row **cannot** make the batched removal delete the wrong songs — strike that sentence, and the "placeholder `Track` to keep indexes correct" half of the fix is unnecessary.

**Severity lowered medium → low:** this is a failed *load*, not data loss. **Scope:** `fetchPlaylistRows` tries the native API first, so on a healthy Navidrome this path never runs for playlists; the favorites path (792) is unconditional and is the live half.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 28, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** ADEQUATE
- **Evidence:** `fetchTracksViaGetSongParallel` (NavidromeClient.swift:910-927) uses `withThrowingTaskGroup` with `for try await track in group` — one throwing child aborts the whole group — and both callers (`fetchFavoriteTracks` line 792, `fetchPlaylistRows` line 1225) call it with plain `try await`, so a single failing `getSong` propagates out and discards everything already parsed in `resolved`/`out`.
- **Better approach:** The core mechanism switch (non-throwing per-id capture, partial success) is correct and matches the sibling `expandFavoriteAlbumTracks` pattern already in the file. But the fix's stated justification for adding a placeholder `Track` is wrong: `navidromeIndex` is not a compacted array position, it's `pair.idx` captured from `for (idx, dict) in entries.enumerated()` over the raw server entry list (`fetchPlaylistRows` line ~1213) and carried straight through to `PlaylistRowItem(..., navidromeIndex: pair.idx)`. Dropping a failed row leaves a hole but does not shift any other row's `navidromeIndex`, and both removal call sites (`AppModel.swift` ~3415-3418, ~4145-4160) consume `row.navidromeIndex` explicitly, never array position — so "a dropped row shifts every later navidromeIndex ... delete the wrong songs" does not hold in this codebase. Better: just skip the failed id in `resolved` (no placeholder needed); this is simpler than fabricating a `Track` from `titleFromPath`.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE — I derived the same refutation (index is anchored to original enumeration, not compacted position) independently before reading the recorded verdict, which reaches the identical conclusion and lowers severity medium→low for the same reason.

## C35 — Widget play/pause intents are a Darwin-notification relay that only works while the app is alive; taps are lost or replayed later
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Widgets/PlayWidgetItemIntent.swift:12–23`; consumer `App/AppModel.swift:2626–2628, 2680–2716`

```swift
private func postWidgetCommand(_ command: String, itemId: String? = nil, itemKind: String? = nil) {
    let defaults = UserDefaults(suiteName: WidgetDataStore.appGroupID)
    defaults?.set(command, forKey: widgetCommandKey)
    if let itemId { defaults?.set(itemId, forKey: widgetCommandPlayIdKey) }
    if let itemKind { defaults?.set(itemKind, forKey: widgetCommandPlayKindKey) }
    defaults?.synchronize()
    CFNotificationCenterPostNotification(
        CFNotificationCenterGetDarwinNotifyCenter(),
        CFNotificationName(widgetCommandNotification),
        nil, nil, true
    )
}
```

**Problem.** Both intents set `openAppWhenRun = false` and run in the widget extension process. A
Darwin notification is delivered only to a **running** process, so if the app was swiped away the tap
does nothing visible. The command then sits in the App Group defaults until the app is next
foregrounded, where `AppModel:2628` drains it "for commands that fired while the app wasn't running" —
so opening the app tomorrow starts playing whatever album the user tapped yesterday. There is no
timestamp, so it cannot be expired. Separately, `writeWidgetData` always writes `kind: .album`
(5858, 5868) even when `id` fell back to `track.id` because `albumId` was empty;
`handleWidgetPlayCommand` then calls `tracks(forAlbumId: trackId)`, gets nothing, and silently returns.

**Fix.** Conform `TogglePlaybackIntent` and `PlayWidgetItemIntent` to `AudioPlaybackIntent` and move
them to the shared target (see **L10**) so `perform()` runs **in the app process** — the system
launches the app in the background for `AudioPlaybackIntent` — then call
`player.togglePlayPause()` / `handleWidgetPlayCommand` directly and delete `postWidgetCommand`, the
Darwin observer and `handleWidgetCommandFromNotification`. If the relay must stay short-term, store
`widgetCommandPostedAt` and discard anything older than 60 s. In `writeWidgetData`, set
`kind: track.albumId.isEmpty ? .track : .album` and handle `.track` by playing the single track.


**Verified —** Both intents confirmed `openAppWhenRun = false` and plain `AppIntent` — no `AudioPlaybackIntent`, `ForegroundContinuableIntent` or `LiveActivityIntent` conformance — so `perform()` runs in the widget extension. Invoked from `Button(intent:)` at 8 sites across both widgets. The only consumer is the `CFNotificationCenterAddObserver` registered from `init`, and Darwin notifications are not queued for a non-running process. No expiry: `grep` for `widgetCommandPostedAt|postedAt` returns nothing, and the drain path reads the raw string with no timestamp check. `kind: .album` hardcoded at 5858/5868 while the id falls back to `track.id`, and `handleWidgetPlayCommand` then calls `tracks(forAlbumId:)` and returns silently on empty — **and it ignores `itemKind` entirely**, which is plumbed widget → defaults → 2710 → 2662 and never read. That last point is an extra defect the entry misses.

**One fix correction:** "move them to the shared target (see L10)" — **they are already in the shared target.** `PlayWidgetItemIntent.swift` is in `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Widgets/` and the pbxproj links `VellumMusicKit` into both targets. Only the `AudioPlaybackIntent` conformance is needed; no file move. Deployment target 26.1 is well past the iOS 17 floor. **Scope:** the silent case narrows to a *recently-played* tile whose track had an empty `albumId` and is not the active track.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 28, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** ADEQUATE
- **Evidence:** `TogglePlaybackIntent`/`PlayWidgetItemIntent` (PlayWidgetItemIntent.swift) both set `public static var openAppWhenRun: Bool = false` and only conform to `AppIntent`, calling `postWidgetCommand` which writes to `UserDefaults(suiteName:)` and fires `CFNotificationCenterPostNotification`. `AppModel.handleAppBecameActive` (line 2626) calls `handleWidgetCommandFromNotification()` "for commands that fired while the app wasn't running" with no timestamp anywhere (`grep` for `widgetCommandPostedAt` returns nothing). Also confirmed the secondary bug: `writeWidgetData` hardcodes `kind: .album` at both sites (`let id = track.albumId.isEmpty ? track.id : track.albumId` then `kind: .album`), and `handleWidgetPlayCommand(itemId:itemKind:)` never references its own `itemKind` parameter in its body at all — it's dead/unused end to end.
- **Better approach:** `AudioPlaybackIntent` conformance is the correct API for this. But "move them to the shared target" is describing something already true: `PlayWidgetItemIntent.swift` already lives in `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Widgets/`, and that package is already linked into both the main app and the widget extension (confirmed via grep — the file is referenced from both `AppModel.swift` and the `VellumWidgets` extension files). No file move is needed or possible to "do" differently — just add the protocol conformance in place.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE — the recorded verdict makes the identical correction ("they are already in the shared target ... no file move") that I reached independently, plus flags the same unused-`itemKind` defect I found.

## C36 — Overlapping widget artwork caches prune each other's files
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** low · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Widgets/WidgetDataStore.swift:108–127`; caller `App/AppModel.swift:5886–5891`

```swift
            if FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: dest.path) { continue }
            var request = URLRequest(url: url)
            request.timeoutInterval = 20
            if let (data, _) = try? await URLSession.shared.data(for: request) {
                try? data.write(to: dest, options: .atomic)
                wrote = true
            }
        }
        pruneArtworkCache(keeping: items)
        return wrote
```

**Problem.** `writeWidgetData()` runs on every `onTrackStarted`, play/pause and recent-play change, and
each spawns `Task.detached { await WidgetDataStore.cacheArtwork(items:) }` with no serialization.
Skipping through a few tracks produces N concurrent runs, each ending with
`pruneArtworkCache(keeping: items)` for **its own (older) payload** — so run 1 deletes the file run 3
just wrote for the current now-playing item, then run 3 returns `wrote == true` and reloads the
timeline, which renders without art. This is the "widget art missing after a skip" symptom. Related to
**E04**, which is about how often this path runs at all.

**Fix.** Serialize through one `actor WidgetArtworkCacher` that coalesces: keep a `pending` items array
and one running task; a new call replaces `pending` and returns if a run is in flight; the run loops
until `pending` is empty and prunes **once**, against the latest set.


**Verified —** Read the omitted `pruneArtworkCache` body (127–136) and it does what the claim says: it enumerates the **whole shared directory** and deletes anything outside its own captured `items`, with no epoch or mtime guard. Concurrency is genuinely unserialized — `WidgetDataStore` is a bare `public enum` with `static` funcs and **zero** hits for `actor|@MainActor|DispatchQueue|NSLock` in the file; the caller fires `Task.detached(.utility)` per call with no coalescing token, from 6 sites including two Combine sinks that fire on every track change and every `isPlaying` flip. Each download carries a 20 s timeout, so an early run easily outlives a later one and prunes its files. Severity `low` is right — the next `cacheArtwork` re-downloads, so it self-heals; the visible cost is one timeline reload rendered without art. **Excerpt defect:** the header cites 108–127 but the block stops at 122, so `pruneArtworkCache` — the crux — is never shown.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 28, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** BEST
- **Evidence:** `WidgetDataStore.cacheArtwork(items:)` ends with `pruneArtworkCache(keeping: items)` (WidgetDataStore.swift ~118), and `pruneArtworkCache` deletes any file in the shared directory not in its own `items` list with no epoch/mtime guard. The caller (`AppModel.swift` ~5885-5891) does `Task.detached(priority: .utility) { let wrote = await WidgetDataStore.cacheArtwork(items: allItems) ... }` on every call to `writeWidgetData()`, which itself fires from at least 6 sites including two Combine `.sink` callbacks (lines 1043, 1053) that trigger on every track-start/play-state change — with no serialization token (`WidgetDataStore` is a bare `enum` with only `static` funcs).
- **Better approach:** N/A — an actor that coalesces `pending` items and loops until empty, pruning once against the final set, is a standard and correct way to serialize this without losing work or reintroducing the race.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE.

## C37 — The schema stamp guards two of the five stores that persist `Track`
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Playback/PlaybackQueueStore.swift:40–47`

```swift
    static func load() -> PlaybackQueueSnapshot? {
        guard let url = try? fileURL(),
              FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: url.path),
              let data = try? Data(contentsOf: url),
              let snap = try? JSONDecoder().decode(PlaybackQueueSnapshot.self, from: data)
        else { return nil }
        return snap
    }
```

**Problem.** `PersistedModelSchema` exists precisely because a file written before a field existed
decodes with `nil` and the app then runs on data that structurally cannot answer the question. That
gate is applied to `LibrarySnapshotStore` and `PlaylistRowsCacheStore` **only**.
`PlaybackQueueSnapshot` (three `[Track]` arrays), `OfflineManifestPayload.records` (which has its own
`version: Int = 4` that `loadManifest` never compares) and `recentlyPlayedTracks` (`[Track]` JSON in
`UserDefaults`) all bypass it. The restored queue is the most visible surface in the app: after an
upgrade, Now Playing → "Go to Artist" on the resumed track and every History row still falls back to
name matching — compounding **C10**. Downloaded tracks are served from the manifest's `Track` forever,
so offline artist links never gain the new fields.

**Fix.** Add `var schemaVersion: Int = 0` to `PlaybackQueueSnapshot` and reject in `load` the way
`LibrarySnapshotStore.load` does — or better, persist only track ids plus position and re-hydrate via
`indexedTrack(id:)` / `tracks(forAlbumId:)` on restore, which also shrinks the file ~3× and helps
**E01**. In `loadManifest`, compare `m.version` against a constant and run a one-time re-hydration of
`records[*].track` when it is behind. Stamp `recentlyPlayedTracks` the same way or store ids only.


**Verified —** `PersistedModelSchema` (`static let current = 1`) is referenced from exactly two stores — 7 grep hits total: 1 definition, 3 in `LibrarySnapshotStore`, 3 in `PlaylistRowsCacheStore`. **Two of five, confirmed.** `PlaybackQueueSnapshot` holds the three `[Track]` arrays as stated plus `userQueuedTrackIds`, with no `schemaVersion` and no gate in `load()`. `OfflineManifestPayload.version = 4` exists at line 90 and `loadManifest()` never references it. `loadRecentlyPlayedTracksFromDefaults` does a bare `decode([Track].self)`. Refutation attempted: there is **no** re-hydration on restore — `restorePlaybackQueueFromDisk()` is two lines with no `indexedTrack(id:)` pass — and the queue is re-saved from the already-`nil`-`artistId` in-memory tracks, so the staleness is sticky exactly as described. **Nuance in the entry's favour:** `LibrarySnapshot` is at least cleared on identity change; `playback-queue.json` gets no equivalent treatment.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 28, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** BEST
- **Evidence:** `grep -rn "PersistedModelSchema"` shows it used only in `LibrarySnapshotStore` and `PlaylistRowsCacheStore` (`guard snap.schemaVersion >= PersistedModelSchema.current else { return nil }`). `PlaybackQueueStore.load()` (lines 40-47, quoted in the finding) has no such gate. `OfflineManifestPayload.version: Int = 4` (OfflineDownloadManager.swift:90) is confirmed never compared in `loadManifest()` (lines 241-254 — decodes and returns directly). `Track.artistId` is documented in-file as "Optional so existing persisted snapshots keep decoding: a missing key reads as `nil` rather than failing the whole snapshot" (MusicLibraryProviding.swift ~265), which independently corroborates the exact failure mode the finding describes for old persisted `Track` data.
- **Better approach:** N/A — adding `var schemaVersion: Int = 0` and gating `load()` mirrors the existing, working pattern in `LibrarySnapshotStore`/`PlaylistRowsCacheStore` exactly; `indexedTrack(id:)` (AppModel.swift:310) exists and is O(1), supporting the "persist ids only, rehydrate" alternative the finding also offers.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE.

## C38 — The magic-playlist id is cached in two places and the name-drift path clears only one
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** low · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/App/AppModel.swift:1690–1692, 2117–2121`

```swift
            if !expectedNames.contains(fetch.name), !LibraryMembership.isMagicPlaylistName(fetch.name) {
                // Name drift (user renamed the magic playlist via web UI). Re-resolve from scratch.
                LibraryMembership.clearCachedPlaylistId(
                    backend: backendKind, serverKey: identity.serverKey, userKey: identity.userKey,
                )
```

**Problem.** `LibrarySnapshot.libraryMagicPlaylistId` (a file, **not** server-scoped) and
`LibraryMembership.cachedPlaylistId` (UserDefaults, scoped by backend/server/user) both hold "the id".
`applyRestoredSnapshotLight` restores the snapshot copy first on cold launch, and the drift handler
clears only the defaults copy. If the user renames or deletes the magic playlist in the web UI, the
next cold launch paints the stale id from the snapshot, and any mutation landing before
`refreshLibraryMembership` completes writes tracks into the renamed — now **user-visible** — playlist,
or fails. Given CLAUDE.md's note that the magic-playlist filter is "a safety boundary, not cosmetics",
an id pointing at the wrong playlist is a real hazard.

**Fix.** Keep one cache. Remove `libraryMagicPlaylistId` from `LibrarySnapshot` (leave the field
optional for decode compatibility, stop writing it) and have `applyRestoredSnapshotLight` read
`LibraryMembership.cachedPlaylistId(...)` for the identity in play, so `clearCachedPlaylistId`
invalidates the only copy. Alternatively gate every mutation entry point on
`hasResolvedMembershipThisSession`.


**Verified —** The facts hold — two unscoped/scoped caches, snapshot seeding at 1690–1692, drift handler clearing only the defaults copy.

**But the causal chain is refuted and the primary fix does not work.** `resolveMagicPlaylistId:2179–2216` does **find-by-name first** (2188) and consults the cached id only as a *third* fallback (2205, itself validated by `isMagicPlaylistName`). So `clearCachedPlaylistId` is near-redundant, and moving `applyRestoredSnapshotLight` onto `cachedPlaylistId` — the entry's primary fix — would seed from a copy that can be **equally stale**, changing nothing. A rename also does not change the playlist's id, so the two copies hold the *same* id; divergence is transient anyway, since the drift handler re-resolves and `applyMagicPlaylistFetch` overwrites the in-memory id.

**The real hazard is the entry's *alternative*, and it is worse than stated.** Nothing gates mutations: `hasResolvedMembershipThisSession` has **zero** hits, and `isResolvingLibraryMembership` has one consumer — a spinner — which is dead on this very path, because `let isInitialResolve = libraryMagicPlaylistId == nil` (2100) evaluates **false** on a cold launch with a snapshot. So the UI shows a fully-resolved library while ~30 ungated call sites read a possibly-stale id. **Rewrite the Problem around the ungated cold-launch window and promote the "Alternatively" clause to *the* fix.** **Excerpt:** only the second of two cited sites is shown.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 29, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** PARTLY REAL · **Fix:** WRONG
- **Evidence:** The two-cache fact is true: `LibrarySnapshot.libraryMagicPlaylistId` lives in a single global file (`private static let filename = "library-snapshot.json"`, no server/user scoping) while `LibraryMembership.cachedPlaylistId` is scoped UserDefaults, and the drift handler at AppModel.swift:2115-2119 calls only `LibraryMembership.clearCachedPlaylistId(...)`. But `resolveMagicPlaylistId` (AppModel.swift:2179-2216) does find-by-name **first** (`for name in candidateNames { if let existing = try await findMagicPlaylistByName(name) { ... return existing } }`) and only falls back to `LibraryMembership.cachedPlaylistId(...)` as a third-tier fallback after the legacy-migration check — so the cached copy the drift handler clears is nearly irrelevant to resolution, and swapping the snapshot's source to that same cache (the proposed fix) doesn't close anything. The real, worse hazard is that ~30 mutation call sites (e.g. `addAlbumToLibrary`: `guard let playlistId = libraryMagicPlaylistId, let lib = activeLibrary else { return }`) read `libraryMagicPlaylistId` completely ungated: `grep -rn hasResolvedMembershipThisSession` returns zero hits anywhere in Sources/Tests/VellumMusicHost, and `isResolvingLibraryMembership`'s only consumer is a spinner in `LibraryView.swift:390` — dead as a gate on this exact path because `let isInitialResolve = libraryMagicPlaylistId == nil` (line 2100) is false on a cold launch that already painted a snapshot id.
- **Better approach:** Don't touch which cache the snapshot mirrors (it changes nothing, since `resolveMagicPlaylistId` barely consults the cached id). Implement the fix's own "alternative" for real: add a `hasResolvedMembershipThisSession` (or reuse `libraryMagicPlaylistId != nil && lastLibraryMembershipRefresh != nil`) flag and gate every mutation entry point (`addAlbumToLibrary`, `removeAlbumFromLibrary`, `toggleFavoriteTrack`, etc.) on it, so a cold-launch snapshot id can paint the UI instantly without being usable for a server write until `refreshLibraryMembership()` actually completes once this session.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE — CODE_SWEEP's Verified block reaches the same two conclusions independently verifiable in the code: the causal chain (name-drift → stale cache → hazard) is refuted by `resolveMagicPlaylistId`'s find-by-name-first order, and the real hazard is the ungated mutation window, backed by the same zero-hit / dead-spinner evidence I confirmed myself.

## C39 — Re-downloading a track permanently names the new file "… (2).ext"
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** low · **Verdict:** **DENIED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Offline/OfflineDownloadManager.swift:714–726`

```swift
        let root = try Self.downloadsFolder()
        let relative = Self.uniqueStructuredRelativePath(for: track, ext: ext, root: root)
        let candidate = root.appendingPathComponent(relative)
        let dest = try Self.containmentCheck(dest: candidate, root: root)

        try removeExistingDownload(for: track.id)
```

**Problem.** `uniqueStructuredRelativePath` probes the disk and appends `(2)` when the canonical name is
taken; only **afterwards** does `removeExistingDownload(for:)` delete the previous file for this track.
So any re-download — after `retryQueueItem`, after a format change, after the **C17** stale-id remap —
lands as `01 Title (2).flac` even though `01 Title.flac` was just deleted, and the folder accumulates
numbered duplicates. The `fileExists`/`removeItem` pair at 723–725 is also redundant with the
unique-path probe two lines earlier.

**Fix.** Call `try removeExistingDownload(for: track.id)` **before** `uniqueStructuredRelativePath`, and
drop the redundant `fileExists`/`removeItem` pair (keep the second `containmentCheck`).


**Verified —** **The ordering observation is correct; the stated consequence is false.** `removeExistingDownload` deletes the file at `payload.tracks[trackId]` — this track's *previous* path — every time. Trace the state machine: **State A** (manifest → `01 Title.flac`, present): the probe sees it, returns `01 Title (2).flac`; 719 deletes the original; result `(2)`. **State B** (manifest → `01 Title (2).flac`, canonical name now free): the probe's first candidate is free, returns the **canonical** name; 719 deletes `(2)`; result canonical. So the name **oscillates** canonical ↔ `(2)`. It is not "permanent", and the folder does **not** accumulate numbered duplicates — there is exactly one file per track id at all times.

Two of the three named triggers also fail: a **format change** yields a different extension so the probe never collides and the file lands canonically named; and the **C17 stale-id remap** goes through `remapDownloadedTrackId(from:to:)`, which rekeys the manifest first, so `removeExistingDownload(for: newId)` does find the old file.

What remains is cosmetic and intermittent — *every other* re-download of the same track in the same format carries a `(2)` suffix. The ordering fix is still worth doing and is correct (the probe still guards the real collision case of two distinct track ids mapping to one structured path), but the finding as written mis-describes the symptom and should be rewritten before it is actioned, not accepted as stated.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 01, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** PARTLY REAL · **Fix:** ADEQUATE
- **Evidence:** The ordering is exactly as quoted (OfflineDownloadManager.swift:714–719): `let relative = Self.uniqueStructuredRelativePath(for: track, ext: ext, root: root)` precedes `try removeExistingDownload(for: track.id)`, and `uniqueStructuredRelativePath` (340–353) is a plain `while FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: dest.path)` probe that appends ` (\(n))`. But the stated symptom is unreachable for the cited triggers, and I do not think the prior pass's oscillation model works either: `cache(track:remote:headers:)` opens with `if downloadedTrackIds.contains(trackId), localFile(for: trackId) != nil { return }` (line 651), and `downloadedTrackIds` is set from `Self.manifestTrackIds()` (182, 531), so the state "manifest maps this id to `01 Title.flac` and that file is present" returns early and never reaches the probe at all. `remapDownloadedTrackId(from:to:)` (1343) rekeys the manifest and keeps the file, so no re-download follows a stale-id swap; a format change yields a different `ext` and therefore a different path. The genuinely reachable `(2)` case is an **orphan** at the canonical path that no manifest entry references (e.g. a crash between `moveItem` and `saveManifest`), and reordering does not help there because `removeExistingDownload(for:)` only deletes `payload.tracks[trackId]`.
- **Better approach:** Do the reorder — it is free and makes the code read correctly — but to actually stop stray `(2)` files, pass the manifest into the probe: `uniqueStructuredRelativePath(for:ext:root:referencedPaths:)` where `referencedPaths` is `Set(payload.tracks.values)` minus this track's own entry, and only bump `(n)` when the occupying file is in that set; an unreferenced file at the canonical path is orphaned garbage and should be overwritten (the `moveItem` already needs the `fileExists`/`removeItem` pair for that, so keep it rather than deleting it as the fix proposes — it is the only thing that makes overwriting legal).
- **Denial:** HOLDS — the title claims a permanent, accumulating rename that the code cannot produce through any of the three named triggers, so the entry should be rewritten before it is actioned.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE on the verdict, DISAGREE on its reasoning — the verifier's "State A" (manifest → `01 Title.flac`, present) is blocked by the early return at line 651, so the described canonical↔`(2)` oscillation cannot occur either; the real residue is untracked orphan files, which neither the finding nor the denial identifies.

## C40 — The EQ tap assumes non-interleaved Float32 without checking the format it was prepared with
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** low _(was medium)_ · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Equalizer/EqualizerAudioTap.swift:417–438` (`tapPrepare`), 485–499 (`tapProcess`)

```swift
    for (bufferIndex, buffer) in buffers.enumerated() {
        guard bufferIndex < Int(state.pointee.channels),
              let raw = buffer.mData
        else { continue }
        let samples = raw.assumingMemoryBound(to: Float.self)
        let channelBase = bufferIndex * bandCount
```

**Problem.** `tapPrepare` records only `mSampleRate` and `mChannelsPerFrame`; it never inspects
`mFormatFlags` or `mBitsPerChannel`. `tapProcess` then treats every buffer as one channel of `Float`.
If the processing format is ever interleaved (one buffer, `mNumberChannels == 2`), the loop runs the
biquad over L,R,L,R as a single stream — the filter state alternates between channels and the output is
garbled stereo at half the intended frequency scale; if it is 16- or 24-bit integer, reinterpreting as
`Float` is noise. AVPlayer taps are Float32 non-interleaved in practice today, but nothing in the code
establishes that, and the check costs nothing on the render path. There is also no guard that
`buffer.mDataByteSize >= frames * 4`, so a short buffer would be over-read.

**Fix.** In `tapPrepare`, compute
`let usable = (format.mFormatFlags & kAudioFormatFlagIsFloat) != 0 && (format.mFormatFlags & kAudioFormatFlagIsNonInterleaved) != 0 && format.mBitsPerChannel == 32`
and pass it to `didPrepare`; when false set `state.pointee.channels = 0` so `tapProcess` falls through
as pure passthrough, and log the flags. In `tapProcess`, add
`frames <= Int(buffer.mDataByteSize) / MemoryLayout<Float>.size` to the per-buffer guard.


**Verified —** The assertion is true: `tapPrepare` touches only `mSampleRate`, `mChannelsPerFrame` and `maxFrames` on both branches, `didPrepare` stores exactly those three, and `grep` for `mFormatFlags|mBitsPerChannel|mDataByteSize` in the file returns **zero hits**. The only per-buffer guard is `bufferIndex < channels` and non-nil `mData`, then `assumingMemoryBound(to: Float.self)` — no size bound. The file is live (reached from `PlaybackEngine` via `TapPlayerItem` at six sites), and worth noting this contradicts CLAUDE.md's "AVPlayer cannot host `AVAudioUnitEQ`" framing: there is a live `MTAudioProcessingTap` EQ path the doc does not mention.

**Two corrections.** The interleaved description is off: with one buffer of `mNumberChannels == 2`, `frames` is frames *per channel*, so the loop would filter only the **first half** of the interleaved buffer and leave the rest untouched — a different artifact than "L,R,L,R as a single stream". And the entry itself concedes AVPlayer taps are Float32 non-interleaved in practice; nothing establishes a path producing another format. **Severity lowered medium → low** — this is defensive hardening against a hypothetical, not a reachable defect. The fix is correct and cheap. **Excerpt defect:** `tapPrepare`, the primary subject, is never shown.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 29, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** BEST
- **Evidence:** `tapPrepare` (EqualizerAudioTap.swift) only ever stores `state.pointee.sampleRate = format.mSampleRate; state.pointee.channels = Int32(format.mChannelsPerFrame); state.pointee.maxFrames = ...` (both the owned and orphan branches) and never reads `format.mFormatFlags` or `format.mBitsPerChannel` — `grep -n "mFormatFlags\|mBitsPerChannel\|mDataByteSize" Sources/VellumMusicKit/Equalizer/EqualizerAudioTap.swift` returns nothing. `tapProcess`'s per-buffer guard is only `guard bufferIndex < Int(state.pointee.channels), let raw = buffer.mData else { continue }` before `raw.assumingMemoryBound(to: Float.self)` and a `for frame in 0 ..< frames` read/write loop with no `mDataByteSize` bound check.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE — CODE_SWEEP confirms the same code facts verbatim and calls the fix "correct and cheap." It also corrects the finding's failure-mode description (an interleaved buffer would only get its first half filtered, not "L,R,L,R as a single stream") and downgrades severity medium→low as defensive hardening against a currently-unreached format; that's a reasonable refinement of consequence, not of whether the missing validation itself exists.

## C41 — `allTracks` swallows the `search3` error and falls back to a 2,000-album walk; `tracksPage` probes three queries at end-of-list
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** low · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Sources/VellumMusicKit/Backends/NavidromeClient.swift:322–328, 349–366`

```swift
    func allTracks(limit: Int) async throws -> [Track] {
        let cap = max(1, min(limit, 50_000))
        if let batch = try? await fetchSongsViaSearch3(cap: cap), !batch.isEmpty {
            return Array(batch.prefix(cap))
        }
        return try await allTracksByWalkingAlbums(limit: cap)
    }
```

**Problem.** `try?` turns an auth rejection or a timeout on one `search3` call into "server has no songs
via search", after which `allTracksByWalkingAlbums` issues `albums(limit: 2000)` and then up to 2,000
`getAlbum` calls in groups of eight — **against a server that just failed**. Cancellation is lost
inside the walk too: `(try? await self.tracks(...)) ?? []` maps `CancellationError` to `[]` and the loop
keeps spawning. Separately `tracksPage` (the Library → Songs paginator) loops `["*", "a", ""]` and stops
only on a non-empty page, so reaching the true end of the list costs three round-trips — and if the
three queries ever rank differently, the page at a given offset can come from a different result set
than the previous page.

**Fix.** Let `fetchSongsViaSearch3` errors propagate (`try await`), falling back to the album walk only
when the call *succeeded* with zero rows. Inside the walk, check `Task.isCancelled` per chunk and throw
`CancellationError()`. In `tracksPage`, probe only on the first page, remember the winning query in
`private var songListQuery: String?`, and reuse it for later offsets so pages come from one ordering
and an empty page means end-of-list in one request.


**Verified —** **The `allTracks` half fully holds, and one detail is worse than stated.** `fetchSongsViaSearch3` does `try await` on the **first** query and lets it throw, so a 401 or a timeout on `"*"` aborts before `"a"` or `""` are tried — `try?` → nil → album walk. `albumBudget = min(2_000, max(400, cap))` and the live caller passes 50,000, so it really is `albums(limit: 2000)` then up to 2,000 `getAlbum` calls in groups of 8, against a server that just failed. Cancellation loss confirmed verbatim, with no `Task.isCancelled` anywhere in 368–393. Both `allTracks` call sites are user-visible (`refreshLibraryTrackMatchIndex`; the add-tracks picker).

**The `tracksPage` half must be re-scoped.** The code is as described, but it is **not** "the Library → Songs paginator" — `grep -rn tracksPage` across Sources, host and Tests returns exactly four hits, all declarations (Nav impl, JF impl, protocol requirement, default impl). **Zero call sites.** The "pages from different result sets" hazard is unreachable today; it is dead API surface. Keep the sub-finding as a trap for whoever wires it up, but drop the attribution. The `allTracks` half alone would justify medium given a 2,000-request storm at an already-failing server.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 29, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** PARTLY REAL · **Fix:** ADEQUATE
- **Evidence:** The `allTracks` half is fully real: `if let batch = try? await fetchSongsViaSearch3(cap: cap), !batch.isEmpty { return ... }` converts any error (auth/timeout) on the first `search3` query into a silent fallback to `allTracksByWalkingAlbums`, which calls `albums(limit: albumBudget)` (`min(2_000, max(400, cap))`) then `(try? await self.tracks(forAlbumId: album.id)) ?? []` in groups of 8 — swallowing `CancellationError` too. But the `tracksPage` half's framing as "the Library → Songs paginator" is not real: `grep -rn "tracksPage" Sources Tests VellumMusicHost` returns exactly four hits — the Navidrome impl, the Jellyfin impl, the protocol requirement, and a protocol-extension default — zero call sites anywhere, and `LibrarySongsView.swift` (grep for "Page\|offset\|allTracks\|paginat") has no reference to it at all. The "pages can come from a different result set" defect is real code but currently unreachable dead API surface, not a live paginator bug.
- **Better approach:** The `allTracks` fix (propagate `search3` errors via `try await`, check `Task.isCancelled` per chunk) is correct as written. For `tracksPage`, fixing its internal query-consistency logic is speculative effort spent on code nothing calls — first confirm whether it's meant to be wired into `LibrarySongsView`'s pagination (in which case wire it up and then fix it) or should be deleted as dead code; polishing an unreachable method's correctness without resolving that question doesn't reduce any real risk today.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE — CODE_SWEEP's Verified block makes exactly this correction ("must be re-scoped... it is not the Library → Songs paginator... Zero call sites... dead API surface"), which I independently confirmed via the same grep.

- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** low · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_

```swift
    private func mediaURLWithQueryAuth(_ base: URL, extraQuery: [URLQueryItem]) -> URL {
        // … (elided)

```

**Problem.** The function is named `mediaURLWithQueryAuth` and does the opposite; its own doc block

home instead of seven consumer files. Do this with **L13**/**L16**/**L22**.

The CLAUDE.md sentence is the strongest part of the finding.

## C43 — App and widget ship with mismatched build numbers because `Info.plist` hard-codes them
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `VellumMusicHost/VellumMusicHost/Info.plist:19–20, 32–33` vs `project.pbxproj:496, 508, 560, 569`

```xml
	<key>CFBundleShortVersionString</key>
	<string>1.1</string>
...
	<key>CFBundleVersion</key>
	<string>3</string>
```

```
				CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = 4;
...
				CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = 2;
				MARKETING_VERSION = 1.1;
				PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER = "$(VELLUM_BUNDLE_ID).widgets";
```

**Problem.** `GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE = NO` and the app plist uses literals, so the app's
`CFBundleVersion` is **3** while the project setting says **4** and the widget — whose plist uses
`$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)` — is **2**. App Store Connect rejects uploads where an embedded
extension's `CFBundleVersion` differs from the container app's, so the first archive fails review
mechanics. Bumping the version currently means editing three places that already disagree.

**Fix.** Replace the two literals in the app plist with `$(MARKETING_VERSION)` and
`$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)` (the widget plist already does this). Move `MARKETING_VERSION` and
`CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION` out of the four per-target configuration blocks into
`VellumMusicHost/Config/Signing.xcconfig` (or a new `Version.xcconfig`) so one line governs every
target.


**Verified —** Read from bytes. **App:** `CFBundleShortVersionString` literal `1.1`, `CFBundleVersion` literal **`3`**; pbxproj says `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = 4`. **Widget:** both are `$(…)` variables resolving to `1.1` and **`2`**. Every refutation route closed: `GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE = NO` in **all four** app/widget configs (the two `= YES` belong to the **VellumMusicUITests** target, which ships nothing); `INFOPLIST_FILE` points at the literal plists in all four; **zero `PBXShellScriptBuildPhase` entries in the entire pbxproj**; no `INFOPLIST_PREPROCESS`, no `agvtool`; and nothing in CI or the build script overrides `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION`. The ITMS-90473 mechanic is real. **Nit:** the second excerpt splices line 560 onto 569 with no ellipsis.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 29, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** BEST
- **Evidence:** `VellumMusicHost/Info.plist` has literal `<key>CFBundleShortVersionString</key><string>1.1</string>` and `<key>CFBundleVersion</key><string>3</string>`, while `project.pbxproj` sets `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = 4;` for the app target (both Debug/Release) and `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = 2;` for the widget target, whose own `VellumWidgets/Info.plist` I confirmed uses `<string>$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)</string>` (i.e. resolves to 2). All four app/widget configs have `GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE = NO`, so the app's literal "3" is what actually ships, mismatched against the widget's "2" and the pbxproj's stated "4".
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE — CODE_SWEEP verified the same byte values and closed every refutation route (no shell-script phase, no agvtool, GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE=NO confirmed on all four relevant configs), matching what I found directly. The widget plist already uses `$(MARKETING_VERSION)`/`$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)`, which I confirmed is the exact pattern the fix proposes applying to the app plist too — proven feasible by the sibling target's existing precedent.

## C44 — The team ID the xcconfig says is "intentionally NOT set" is set in the pbxproj
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** medium · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `VellumMusicHost/VellumMusicHost.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:422, 466` vs `VellumMusicHost/Config/Signing.xcconfig:3–6`

```
				DEVELOPMENT_TEAM = F7YZT72GUX;
```

```
// DEVELOPMENT_TEAM is intentionally NOT set here. Each collaborator signs with
// their own Apple Developer team, and committing a team ID means every pull
// overwrites someone else's signing and breaks their build with
// "you don't have access to this membership resource".
```

**Problem.** Both project-level configurations commit the team id. It works today only because the same
`Signing.xcconfig` is also attached at target level (485/520/554/582), where a target-level xcconfig
outranks a project-level build setting. A collaborator who has not created `Local.xcconfig` gets **no
error** — they silently sign against the upstream team and hit exactly the failure the comment
describes. If anyone removes the target-level `baseConfigurationReference` (Xcode's "Convert to
xcconfig" UI does this), `Local.xcconfig` stops having any effect at all.

**Fix.** Delete the two `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM = F7YZT72GUX;` lines from `project.pbxproj`. Add a pre-build
Run Script phase that fails with a clear message when `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` is empty and
`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED` is `YES`, so the intended setup is enforced rather than described.


**Verified —** Exactly two `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` occurrences, both `F7YZT72GUX`, both in the **PBXProject**-level configuration list (Debug 422, Release 466). No target-level config, scheme, script or workflow sets it. The xcconfig comment is verbatim and the file genuinely never assigns it — it only ends with `#include? "Local.xcconfig"`.

**Precedence reasoning is correct, not backwards.** Xcode's order, highest first: target build settings → **target xcconfig** → **project build settings** → project xcconfig → defaults. Target xcconfig (rank 2) does outrank project build settings (rank 3). Attachment confirmed at 485, 520, 554, 582 (and 610, 636 for UITests, which the entry omits, harmless). **Mechanism confirmed exactly:** `#include?` is the *optional* form, so a collaborator with no `Local.xcconfig` gets a silent skip, `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` is undefined at rank 2, and the committed team is inherited at rank 3. Locally `Local.xcconfig` sets a different team, which is why it works here and would not on a fresh clone. Note the project-level configs also reference `Signing.xcconfig` at rank 4 — *below* the hardcoded team — so that include is already dead weight. **Reword:** "gets **no error**" is imprecise; with `CODE_SIGN_STYLE = Automatic` they do get an error, just the opaque "you don't have access to this membership resource" one with no pointer to the missing file. Say "no *configuration* error, only an opaque signing failure."


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 29, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** BEST
- **Evidence:** `grep -n "DEVELOPMENT_TEAM" project.pbxproj` returns exactly two hits, both `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM = F7YZT72GUX;` (lines 422, 466), and both sit inside the project-level (not target-level) `XCBuildConfiguration` blocks — confirmed by their position directly under the first two `baseConfigurationReference = ...Signing.xcconfig` entries in the "Begin XCBuildConfiguration section," before any target-specific blocks. `Signing.xcconfig` itself never sets `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` and ends with `#include? "Local.xcconfig"` (the optional include), matching its own comment that the team id is "intentionally NOT set here."
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE, including its correction to the finding's own wording: CODE_SWEEP points out "gets no error" should be "no *configuration* error, only an opaque signing failure" (with `CODE_SIGN_STYLE = Automatic` there is still a build failure, just an unhelpful Apple one) — I'd independently flag this same wording as an inference worth softening. The precedence claim (target xcconfig ranks above project build settings) is standard, documented Xcode behavior and I found no contradicting evidence in this project.

## C45 — Swift 6.2 tools, but every target pins Swift 5 language mode with no strict concurrency
- **Round:** 2 · **Severity:** low · **Verdict:** **CONFIRMED** _(verify pass, round 2; different agent than the raiser)_
- **File:** `Package.swift:21, 27, 33`; `project.pbxproj:513, 547, 575, 603, 628, 654`

```swift
            swiftSettings: [.swiftLanguageMode(.v5)]
```

**Problem.** CLAUDE.md leans on actor isolation for correctness ("All UI-facing models cross main actor
boundaries. New `Observable` view-state types should be `@MainActor`"), and `AppModel` is reached from
`CFNotificationCenter` callbacks and detached tasks. In Swift 5 mode with no
`SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY`, none of those annotations are checked at the boundary — a non-isolated call
into `AppModel` compiles silently. **This is the setting that lets C19, C20, C21, C27 and C28 exist
without a single diagnostic.** The project is on tools 6.2 already; `.v5` buys only not seeing the
warnings.

**Fix.** Add `.enableUpcomingFeature("StrictConcurrency")` to the `VellumMusicKit` target's
`swiftSettings`, fix warnings file-by-file starting with `App/`, `Playback/`, `Library/`, then flip to
`.swiftLanguageMode(.v6)` and `SWIFT_VERSION = 6.0` in the pbxproj. Do it behind a CI job running with
the flag on and `continue-on-error: true` until the count reaches zero. Treat this as the umbrella task
for the round-2 concurrency findings rather than a cleanup.


**Verified —** Every cited line exact — `.swiftLanguageMode(.v5)` at Package.swift 21/27/33 on tools 6.2, `SWIFT_VERSION = 5.0` at all six pbxproj configs, and **zero** hits for `SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY` / `SWIFT_UPCOMING_FEATURE` / `SWIFT_APPROACHABLE*` anywhere.

**Narrow the mechanism.** "None of those annotations are checked at the boundary — a non-isolated call into `AppModel` compiles silently" overreaches: actor-isolation violations on *direct calls* are diagnosed as errors in Swift 5 mode too (which is exactly why **C49**'s proposed fix would fail to compile). What minimal checking actually suppresses is `Sendable` conformance on values crossing isolation boundaries, non-Sendable captures in `Task`/`@Sendable` closures, and unprotected `static var` global state — i.e. precisely **C48** and **C49**. Rewrite the sentence accordingly; the umbrella framing is still right. **Pick a different exemplar:** the `CFNotificationCenter` callback already hops correctly (`Task { @MainActor in model.handleWidgetCommandFromNotification() }`) and never touches `AppModel` off-main.


**Re-verified (T238) —** independent second pass, agent 30, judged from the source with the first pass's verdict withheld.

- **Problem:** REAL · **Fix:** BEST
- **Evidence:** `Package.swift` lines 21/27/33 all read `swiftSettings: [.swiftLanguageMode(.v5)]` on `// swift-tools-version: 6.2`, and `grep -n "SWIFT_VERSION" project.pbxproj` returns `SWIFT_VERSION = 5.0;` at all six cited lines (513/547/575/603/628/654), with zero hits for `SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY`/`SWIFT_UPCOMING_FEATURE` anywhere in the repo. However the problem text's mechanism overreaches: "none of those annotations are checked at the boundary — a non-isolated call into `AppModel` compiles silently" is false as a blanket claim — direct synchronous calls into an isolated function from a wrong context are a hard actor-isolation error even in Swift 5 mode (this is exactly why C49's proposed `@MainActor` fix fails to compile, see below). What Swift 5 mode actually suppresses is `Sendable`-crossing checks and unprotected `static var` globals (C48/C49's actual shape), not direct-call isolation.
- **Versus the first pass:** AGREE — recorded verdict is CONFIRMED and its own "Narrow the mechanism" correction says precisely what I found independently before reading it (cites C49 as the proof case). Its suggested replacement exemplar (the `CFNotificationCenter` → `Task { @MainActor in ... }` hop) I did not re-verify line-by-line but the substantive point matches my own read.
